# STAGE 1 — THE CANDLE LANGUAGE (revised): tokenizer + non-predictive gate

## 1. What this is, in your terms

We take **one asset's minute OHLC stream** and turn it into a sequence of discrete **tokens**, where each token is a **recurring, variable-length run of candle shapes** described by **relative moves measured in local-volatility units** — so a token carries its own magnitude (a big version and a small version of the same proportional shape are *different* tokens, per your resolved F1), and is invariant to absolute price, scale, position, and location. We are **not predicting anything**: the tokenizer only builds a **vocabulary** — a language of price-action shapes — by finding which relative-shape runs *recur often enough to be worth a word*. Transfer across the 64 assets ($225/unit vs $0.45/unit → same token) is a **structural** consequence of (a) encoding everything as vol-unit ratios and (b) fitting **one shared codebook** on the pooled corpus — never learned cross-asset attention. "Good" is judged the way you'd judge a language/codebook (compresses, covers, recurs, transfers, reconstructs), **with no downstream predictor and no prediction framing anywhere**.

---

## 2. Tokenizer design

### 2.1 Per-bar substrate — vol-unit relative moves (F1: corrected)

The prior draft encoded raw `log(c_t/c_{t-1})` and *skipped* vol-normalization. **That silently overrode resolved fork F1** (TASK_791 L41-43: "each move in local-volatility units, magnitude is part of token identity"). Corrected: every magnitude feature is divided by a **causal local-vol estimate** before binning.

Let `σ_t = EWMA( |log(c/c_{t-1})|, halflife=H )` computed **causally** (only bars ≤ t), re-anchored on the cadence in §2.5. Per bar:

| Feature | Definition | Role |
|---|---|---|
| `mv_t` | `log(c_t / c_{t-1}) / σ_t` | **vol-unit inter-bar move** — the token-identity magnitude axis |
| `gap_t` | `log(o_t / c_{t-1}) / σ_t` | **inter-bar gap** (NEW — minute bars gap, esp. the $0.45 alts; a gap-up-then-flat bar ≠ a grind-up bar) |
| `body_t` | `log(c_t / o_t) / σ_t` | intrabar direction/strength, vol-unit |
| `range_t`| `log(h_t / l_t) / σ_t` | bar extent, vol-unit |
| `uw_t` | `(h_t − max(o,c)) / (h_t − l_t + ε)` | upper-wick fraction ∈[0,1] (already scale-free; no vol norm) |
| `lw_t` | `(min(o,c) − l_t) / (h_t − l_t + ε)` | lower-wick fraction ∈[0,1] |

Note `mv_t ≈ gap_t + body_t` by construction; we keep `gap` and `body` as the two independent axes and derive `mv` for the move-bin. Guard every denominator with `maximum(·, ε)`; clamp `σ_t` to a floor so flat regimes don't blow up vol-units (the SAX flat-window pathology, now relocated to the vol estimate).

**Why this still passes the $225/$0.45 demo:** a pure proportional rescale leaves *both* the log-ratio and `σ_t` unchanged → identical vol-units → identical token. So we lose nothing on transfer and gain F1-compliance: `log(1.25)` on a placid asset vs a frantic asset now land in **different** move-bins, which is what you decided.

### 2.2 Base alphabet — data-adaptive product quantization

Map each bar's vol-unit tuple to a **base symbol** via a product alphabet (1d-SAX generalized):
- **move axis** (`mv_t`): quantile/Lloyd-Max bins fitted on the **pooled** vol-unit distribution (fat-tailed → never Gaussian breakpoints; high-density ranges get finer codes).
- **gap axis** (`gap_t`): coarse signed bins (most bars ≈0; tail matters).
- **body/range axis**: joint quantile bins.
- **wick shape**: coarse 3-way (top-heavy / balanced / bottom-heavy).

Breakpoints are fitted **once on the pooled 64-asset vol-unit corpus** — this single shared bin table is what makes the same shape land on the same symbol across assets. Initial cardinality (set by eval, not hand): move≈8, gap≈3, body/range≈4, wick≈3. Final cardinality by MDL (§4).

### 2.3 Variable-length segmentation (two mechanisms — F3 leans variable)

1. **Numerosity reduction with a run-length tag.** Collapse runs of identical base symbols to one symbol + coarse length tag (`FLAT×short` vs `FLAT×long` stay distinct). This is the symbol-level noise filter.
2. **Frequency-greedy merge (BPE/RePair) over the reduced stream.** Composes short symbols into longer variable-length tokens; boundaries are **frequency-derived, never learned with a reward** (a forecasting-reward patcher would violate the spec). Token bar-length is **emergent**, not a hyperparameter.

### 2.4 "Viable" vs "null" — defined end-to-end (closes the integration seam)

A merge becomes a **viable token** iff it recurs **≥ `p_min`** times across the pooled corpus *and* survives pruning (§2.6). Everything else is **null**. The null run is represented **three ways for three consumers**, reconciled explicitly so nothing breaks:

| Consumer | Null representation |
|---|---|
| **MDL / gate (§4)** | null bars are **coded at full base-symbol entropy cost** (like-for-like vs the raw baseline) — they are *not* free |
| **Stage-2 embedding (§3)** | a single reserved `<NULL>` token occupies the position (keeps bar-position alignment intact) |
| **Trader (§5)** | `<NULL>` runs are **dropped** from the planned sequence (the denoising payoff) |

This resolves the latent contradiction (drop-for-trader vs code-for-MDL vs placeholder-for-embedding): they are *different views of the same null span*, all defined here.

### 2.5 Drift control for a 24/7 corpus (FAPCA, corrected)

`σ_t` and the increment anchor re-anchor on a **fixed minute cadence (every 1440 min / UTC-day), not "per session"** — most of the 64 assets are crypto/FX with **no session boundary**, so "session re-anchor" was undefined for them. Fixed-cadence re-anchoring is well-defined for both session and 24/7 assets.

### 2.6 Build → prune → freeze (one shared codebook)

- **Build:** BPE merge counts **pooled across all 64 assets** → single shared vocabulary (the transfer mechanism). Applied **per-asset independently** at encode time — no cross-asset coupling.
- **Prune:** (a) near-duplicate cluster under **length-normalized z-normed Euclidean** distance (÷√len), keep one canonical per cluster; (b) greedy minimum-cardinality **set-cover** on fraction-of-stream explained.
- **Artifact audit (offline, O(n²), never in the loop):** confirm each token's occurrences are tight under Matrix-Profile/VALMOD on the raw vol-unit windows — kills "tokens" that are binning coincidences.
- **Serving = exact BPE merge ranking, NOT greedy longest-match.** Longest-match produces a *different* segmentation than the merge order that built the vocab and would silently break rescale-invariance at serving time. Add an A0 check at serving (§4).

---

## 3. Stage-2 embedding sketch (non-predictive)

**Objective: masked-token recovery (BERT/word2vec cloze), bidirectional, never causal/forecasting** (TASK_793). Mask a random subset of token IDs; train a bidirectional encoder to classify the masked token from two-sided context. Hidden states → contextual embeddings handed to the trader.

- **Init from codebook structure:** seed the embedding table from each token's canonical vol-unit template (mean per-bar ratios, length), not random.
- **Optional auxiliary:** TS2Vec-style contrastive term on two augmented in-context views; auxiliary only (naive augmentations mint false positives).
- **No cross-asset smuggle (explicit):** masking and attention **must not cross asset-sequence seams** (no document-bleed across concat boundaries); **no asset-ID / positional-asset conditioning**. The embedding space is shared (word-level), but context never straddles assets. *(Flagged now so 793 doesn't drift; gating is out of scope for Stage-1 per TASK_791 L62.)*

---

## 4. Non-predictive eval battery (replaces the next-bar-sign probe)

Frame: **lossy compression + discrete coding.** Every metric is computable from raw token streams, zero labels, zero prediction. Thresholds are starting points to calibrate against baselines + the MDL knee, not literature constants.

### Tier 0 — Correctness pre-gate (cheapest, run first)
- **A0 rescale-invariance.** Re-tokenize a window at a different price scale → token sequence **byte-identical. PASS = 100%.** Run at training *and* at serving (catches the longest-match bug). Hard gate.

### Tier 1 — Transfer (THE headline — it tests the product claim)
Promoted to headline because it's the one gate that tests "cross-asset transferable" and is hardest to game.
- **A8 build-on-A / score-on-B.** Build vocab on a subset; tokenize held-out assets at extreme price levels ($225 vs $0.45) with the *same* codebook. Report mass-weighted coverage of B by tokens that also fire on A, active-vocab Jaccard, **Spearman frequency-rank correlation at mid-frequency**.
  - **Exclude top-k mega-tokens** (a flat/doji token recurs everywhere and fakes overlap) and measure the **mid-frequency** band.
  - **Two controls, both required (satisfies TASK_792's "above a shuffled control"):** real vocab must beat **(i) a per-asset returns-shuffled stream** AND **(ii) a random-merge same-size vocabulary**. Control (ii) is the one that isolates *good merges* from *any merges*.
  - **PASS:** high held-out mid-freq coverage + high mid-freq rank-correlation, beating **both** controls. If this fails, the central promise fails regardless of single-asset MDL.

### Tier 2 — Compression (genuine only after the bit-budget fix)
- **A1 two-part MDL, bits-per-candle, over the FULL stream.**
  `bits = Σ_covered log₂(1/p(token)) + Σ_null (base-symbol entropy cost of the raw bars) + L(boundary positions) + L(codebook)`.
  Null bars **and** segmentation-boundary bits are charged (the prior draft omitted both, which flattered the tokenizer and made the go/no-go un-evaluable when 30%+ of bars are null).
  - **PASS:** strictly below (a) a raw base-symbol entropy coder over the *same full stream* and (b) a **random-merge same-size vocab** — not just below raw. The random-merge baseline is the real bar.
  - **Vocab size is chosen by the A8-transfer-stable region, NOT an eyeballed knee** (the MDL knee is soft on fat-tailed data and a `p_min` floor keeps a self-paying Zipf tail). Report MDL as a curve; let transfer drive `k`.

### Tier 3 — Fidelity
- **A2 reconstruction within ratio-tolerance.** Per occurrence, reconstruct vol-unit ratios from the canonical template; **PASS: ≥90-95% within tolerance**, bounded mean log-ratio MSE. Always paired with A1 (recon-alone monotonically improves with alphabet size). Reward-critical for Stage 3 (phantom decode error → phantom alpha).

### Tier 4 — Variable-length sanity (the only direct test that "shapes emerged")
- **A9 length-distribution non-degeneracy (NEW).** **PASS:** median token length in ~[3, 30]; **no single token covers >X% of bars**; not all length-1. A tokenizer can pass MDL+transfer while degenerating to all-singletons or one mega-token; this is the only gate that catches it.
- **A4 coverage band.** coverage = fraction of bars in a viable (non-null) token. **PASS BAND: 60-70% ≤ coverage, null < 25-40%.** Deliberately **not ~100%** — near-total coverage means we're tokenizing noise and the denoising payoff is gone. Report candles-per-token jointly.

### Tier 5 — Health diagnostics (bands, NEVER maximized)
- **A5 active-code fraction >80%, perplexity not collapsed.** Catches dead-code bloat / mega-token domination.
- **A6 Zipf slope + Rényi efficiency** — **report as health bands only, do NOT maximize** (Rényi is gameable: random-drop BPE raises it while degrading quality). TASK_792 wants "Zipfian" — we confirm the *shape* is Zipf-like as a sanity band, we do not optimize toward it.
- **A7 segmentation stability** under sub-tolerance jitter + small shifts; boundary-F1. **PASS >0.85** (relaxed from 0.9 — causal `σ_t` reacts to a jittered bar, so a stateless-encoder 0.9 was optimistic).

### Why A3 (Persist-vs-shuffle) is DEMOTED, not the headline
A time-shuffle control is **circular**: numerosity reduction + BPE manufacture local self-similarity, and minute returns/vol are autocorrelated, so *any* tokenizer — even a deliberately bad one — beats its own time-shuffle. It tests "does the data have temporal structure" (known), not "is this vocabulary good." It is retained **only** as the cheap shuffled-control input to A8 (which TASK_792 explicitly asks for), never as a standalone proof.

### Verdict rule (re-weighted around the product)
Ship to Stage-2 **iff:**
**A8 transfer (mid-freq, mega-tokens excluded, beats BOTH controls) AND A2 fidelity AND A1 corrected-full-stream MDL beats the random-merge same-size vocab AND A9 non-degenerate length distribution.**
A0 is the cheap correctness pre-gate. Tiers 4-band/5 are advisory. **A3-vs-shuffle dropped as a pillar.**
*Necessary-not-sufficient (honored):* these prove the language is well-formed, recurring, transferable, reconstructible — **not** that tokens carry tradeable meaning. Meaning is strictly Stage-2/3 by design.

---

## 5. Pipeline slot-in + efficiency

- **Online path (O(n), in the loop):** candles → vol-unit ratio features → base symbols (frozen bin table) → numerosity-reduce → **exact-BPE-merge-order** encode against frozen vocab → token IDs. (Matrix-Profile/VALMOD audits stay offline.)
- **Embedding:** each token ID → Stage-2 contextual embedding → fed where raw candle features used to go. `<NULL>` positions carry the reserved embedding so bar-position alignment to the trader is preserved.
- **Denoising payoff:** `<NULL>` runs are **dropped** from the trader's planned sequence; MCTS plans over a shorter, cleaner stream. Token compression of ~2-4× is the externally-reported ballpark for exactly this kind of grammar/BPE compression → faster, denoised training.
- **Safety:** a pure representation swap, MCTS planning untouched; each asset tokenized independently with the shared codebook → no cross-asset coupling introduced.
- **Drift contract:** fixed-cadence (UTC-day) re-anchoring aligns token boundaries to real prices daily for all 64 assets including 24/7.

---

## 6. Cheapest first experiment (CPU-first)

Goal: prove the **language**, not the trader. Entirely CPU/RAM under `tools/safe_run.sh --cpu --mem 64G` (no GPU on workstation). No Stage-2, no MCTS, no forecast.

- **E0 data:** load minute OHLC for the 64 assets from `trading_data.db` into RAM once. Pick ~6 assets spanning the widest price range (literal $225↔$0.45) as **held-out transfer set**; build on the rest.
- **E1 substrate:** vol-unit ratio features (causal `σ_t`, fixed-cadence anchor); fit pooled quantile/Lloyd-Max bins (move/gap/body/range) + coarse wick code.
- **E2 tokenize:** numerosity-reduce (run-length tag) → pooled BPE with floor `p_min`; sweep vocab size; prune (near-dup cluster + set-cover).
- **E3 eval in cost order:** A0 (must be 100%, at train *and* serving) → A8 transfer vs **both** controls (random-merge + returns-shuffle) → A1 corrected full-stream MDL vs random-merge baseline → A2 fidelity → A9 length non-degeneracy → A4/A5/A6 bands. (A7 stability + VALMOD audit are fast-follow.)

**What it proves:** that a vol-unit relative encoding yields a finite, compressive vocabulary whose tokens *recur across assets at wildly different price levels better than matched-complexity random merges* — i.e., the transfer claim is real, with zero predictor.

**Kill / proceed (NOT a predictor):**
- **PROCEED** iff **A8 beats both controls at mid-freq AND A1-corrected beats the random-merge vocab AND A2 ≥90% AND A9 non-degenerate**.
- **KILL** if A8 collapses to a control (encoding isn't actually transferable in practice), or A1-corrected can't beat random-merge once null+boundary bits are charged (no real compression), or the vocab degenerates (A9). None of these is a forecast — they are coding/transfer facts.
- **Sweep order on soft-fail:** `K` (bins) → `p_min`/vocab size (driven by A8-stable region) → run-length tag granularity → wick resolution. Set alphabet-size gates (MDL/transfer) **before** judging coverage — grammar quality is meaningless until the base alphabet is right.

---

## 7. Open design forks — you decide

**F2 — vocabulary discovery method (still open in TASK_789).**
*Statistical frequency-merge (BPE/RePair shared codebook)* **vs** *learned VQ (FSQ, collapse-proof)* **vs** hybrid.
→ **Recommend BPE/RePair as the primary build.** It's CPU-first, prediction-free by construction, serving is deterministic, and it's the only option that makes the whole §6 experiment runnable in hours with no GPU. Keep FSQ as a *named fallback* only if A8 transfer fails for reasons traceable to brittle hard bin boundaries (then a learned soft quantizer might rescue overlap). You leaned "discovered statistical vocabulary" — this matches.

**F3 — segmentation unit (still open in TASK_789).**
*Variable-length emergent (numerosity + BPE)* **vs** *fixed-length patches (PatchTST-style)*.
→ **Recommend variable-length.** Your reference token is explicitly variable-length; fixed patches can't represent "3 up then 1 down then 1.4…" as one unit. Fixed-length is only worth it if A9 shows variable-length degenerating badly — unlikely, but the gate will tell us.

**F4 — what drives vocabulary size `k`.**
*MDL knee* **vs** *A8 transfer-stable region*.
→ **Recommend transfer-stable region drives `k`, MDL reported as a curve.** Transfer is the product claim and the knee is soft on fat-tailed minute data. This is a change from the prior draft (which let the knee pick `k`).

**F5 — run-length tag granularity (the numerosity/precision tradeoff).**
*Collapse blindly (smallest vocab, loses 8-vs-12-flat-bars)* **vs** *coarse length tag (short/med/long — keeps count, bigger vocab)*.
→ **Recommend the coarse 3-bucket tag.** For trading, "flat for 8" vs "flat for 40" minutes is a different regime; blind collapse throws that away. Cheap to widen/narrow during the §6 sweep, so start coarse and let A9/A1 tune it.

---

### Changes vs the prior draft (so you can diff fast)
1. **Encoder now vol-unit** (F1 honored), not raw log-returns; "skip vol-norm" paragraph deleted.
2. **A8 transfer is the headline**, A1 second; **A3-vs-shuffle demoted** to a control input only.
3. **A1 bit budget fixed** — charges null bars + boundary bits over the full stream; baseline is now random-merge vocab, not just raw entropy.
4. **`gap_t` feature added** (minute bars gap).
5. **FAPCA → fixed-cadence (UTC-day) re-anchor** for 24/7 assets.
6. **Null token defined end-to-end** (code-for-MDL / `<NULL>`-for-embedding / drop-for-trader).
7. **A9 length-non-degeneracy gate added.**
8. **Serving = exact BPE merge order**, not greedy longest-match (+ A0-at-serving).
9. **Stage-2 no-cross-asset-seam footnote.**
10. **Vocab size `k` driven by transfer**, not the MDL knee.

Spec refs: `tasks/TASK_791_TOKENIZER_LANGUAGE.md` (F1 resolved, L41-43/48), `TASK_792_LANGUAGE_GATE.md` (shuffled-control requirement, Zipfian wording), `TASK_793_TOKEN_EMBEDDING.md`, `TASK_789_TEMPORAL_TOKEN_MIDDLE_LAYER.md` (F2/F3 open).

# Adversarial critique: "The Candle Language" design vs. SPEC

## VERDICT IN ONE LINE
The spine (relative encoding → numerosity reduction → BPE → compression/transfer gates) is sound and spec-legal. But the design **contradicts the one fork the operator already RESOLVED** (F1 amplitude → vol-unit, not log-return), and its headline structural gate (A3 Persist) is **trivially passable by construction**, meaning the eval does NOT prove "the language is right." Two load-bearing fixes below, plus several smaller ones.

---

## (0) HARD CONTRADICTION WITH THE COMMITTED SPEC — the proposal ignores a resolved fork

This is the single most important finding and it is not a matter of taste. `TASK_791` line 41–43 records:

> **F1 RESOLVED → (A) vol-unit magnitude** — each move in local-volatility units, magnitude is part of token identity; invariance comes from vol-unit normalization, not from discarding amplitude. (Encoder normalizes by local vol, NOT full per-window z-norm of magnitude.)

The proposal §1.1 instead encodes `r_t = log(c_t/c_{t-1})` **raw**, and §1.1's "No per-window z-norm" paragraph proudly argues invariance "for free" from log-returns. It never divides by local volatility. **This is a different encoder than the one the operator signed off on**, and the difference is material, not cosmetic:

- The operator's intent (vol-unit) is that `log(1.25)` on a placid asset and `log(1.25)` on a frantic asset are **different tokens** because magnitude is relative to *local regime*, not absolute. The proposal's raw-log encoding makes them the **same** token. One of these is wrong for this project, and the spec already decided: it's the proposal.
- Worse, the proposal's "$225 vs $0.45 → same token" demonstration (§1.5 Step E) only works because it uses raw log-returns. Under the resolved vol-unit scheme, the demo's correctness still holds (a proportional rescale leaves vol-units unchanged), so the proposal **didn't even need** to drop vol-normalization to pass its own showcase. It dropped a resolved design decision for no demonstrated gain.

**Concrete fix:** Re-derive the substrate as `r_t / σ_local(t)` where `σ_local` is a causal local-vol estimate (e.g., rolling MAD/EWMA of `|r|` over the prior N minutes, re-anchored per session to match the FAPCA boundary). Then quantile-bin the vol-unit move. This is a one-line change to §1.1 but it changes every downstream bin, every token, and every eval number. The proposal must be rejected and resent on this basis alone, OR the operator must explicitly re-open F1. Silently overriding a `✅ RESOLVED` fork is the worst failure mode here.

Second-order consequence the proposal missed: with **causal local-vol normalization**, A0 (rescale-invariance) is still exact, but A7 (jitter stability) gets *harder* because `σ_local` reacts to the jittered bar. The proposal's A7 threshold (boundary-F1 > 0.9) was set for a stateless encoder and is now optimistic.

---

## (1) Smuggled prediction / circular eval — the structural gate is trivially passable

The user threw out the next-bar-sign probe and demanded a non-predictive gate that actually **proves the language is good**. The proposal's designated replacement is **A3: Persist self-transition KL, real stream vs. time-shuffled control** (§3 Tier 3, called "the true replacement for the sign-probe" and "the primary no-predictor structural gate").

**A3 is circular and near-guaranteed to pass regardless of vocabulary quality.** Here's the mechanism:

- Persist measures self-transition persistence: P(next token == current token) vs. marginal. The token stream is built by **numerosity reduction + BPE**, both of which **manufacture local self-similarity and merge frequent adjacencies into single symbols**. After numerosity reduction, identical-run collapse *removes* trivial self-transitions, but BPE then creates a stream whose adjacent tokens are, by selection, the most frequent co-occurring pairs.
- Now shuffle in time. You destroy adjacency. Of course Persist/any-temporal-structure score drops to ~0. **A shuffled control beating the real stream is mathematically almost impossible for ANY tokenizer over autocorrelated minute data** — even a deliberately bad one (e.g., random equiprobable bins with no merges) will beat its own shuffle, because minute log-returns and volatility are autocorrelated. The shuffle control tests "does my data have *any* temporal structure," which we already know it does. It does **not** test "is *this vocabulary* good."

So A3-vs-shuffle is the same category of error as the sign-probe: a strawman control that the design passes by construction. It is non-predictive, yes — but "non-predictive" was never the only requirement; "**proves the language is right**" was.

**Concrete fixes (need at least one, ideally both):**
1. **Replace the shuffle control with a *vocabulary* control, not a *time* control.** Compare the real vocabulary against (a) a **random-merge BPE** (merge random adjacent pairs to the same vocab size) and (b) a **frequency-matched random codebook**. The real vocabulary must beat *these matched-complexity alternatives* on MDL/coverage/transfer — that isolates "good merges" from "any merges." Shuffling time only isolates "any structure."
2. **Predictability of the *token stream by its own grammar*, label-free:** measure the **conditional entropy H(token_t | context) under a simple count-based n-gram over tokens** vs. the same over a random-merge vocab. A good language has lower per-token conditional entropy *for a given vocab size* — this is compression, not forecasting (no external target, no price label), and it's the actual operationalization of "the tokens form a language." The proposal gestures at this inside A1 (MDL) but then over-weights A3, which is the weaker test.

The verdict rule (§3) requires "A3 Persist-beats-shuffle" as a mandatory gate. **Remove it or replace its control.** As written, it is a free pass dressed as a structural proof.

---

## (2) The single weakest link that makes the language un-evaluable: A1's baselines are underspecified and gameable

A1 (MDL bits-per-candle) is named "the headline." Its pass condition is "strictly below BOTH (a) a raw-candle entropy coder AND (b) a fixed-length n-gram tokenizer." Two problems make this the weakest evaluative link:

- **"Raw-candle entropy coder" is undefined and the comparison is apples-to-oranges.** Bits-per-candle for the token stream counts `−Σ log₂ p(token) + L(codebook)`. But a token spans a *variable, emergent* number of candles. To get bits-*per-candle* you must divide by candles-covered — and **uncovered/fallback candles (A4 says 30–40% of them!) have to be coded too**, or you're comparing the compression of the easy 60% against a baseline that codes 100%. The proposal never says how fallback candles enter the bit budget. If they're excluded, A1 is rigged in the tokenizer's favor; if they're included at raw cost, A1 may *never* beat the baseline once 30%+ of the stream is paying full entropy. **This ambiguity alone can flip the go/no-go either way — it is the un-evaluable core.**
  - **Fix:** define the bit budget over the **entire stream**: `bits = Σ_covered log₂(1/p(token)) + Σ_fallback (cost of coding the raw bar) + L(codebook) + L(boundary positions)`. Code fallback bars with the *same* base-symbol entropy coder used in baseline (a), so it's a true like-for-like. Include **boundary/segmentation bits** — variable-length tokenization must pay to encode where tokens start, and the proposal omits this, which silently flatters the tokenizer.

- **MDL "knee selects vocabulary size" can be gamed by the very dead-code the design claims to avoid.** Standard pitfall (the proposal cites it for A6 but not A1): two-part MDL with a frequency-floor `p_min` will happily keep a long Zipf tail of rare-but-real tokens that *barely* pay for themselves, inflating `L(codebook)` while shaving a hair off `L(data)`. The "knee" is often soft/absent on fat-tailed financial data. **Fix:** report MDL as a curve and pick vocab by the cross-asset-transfer-stable region (A8), not by an eyeballed knee — i.e., let §3 Tier 6 *drive* vocab size, since transfer is the actual product claim.

---

## (3) Drift from minute granularity / relative-transferability — mostly clean, two leaks

- **Leak A — `r_t = log(c_t/c_{t-1})` is close-to-close and throws away the open-gap, which is huge on minute data.** Minute bars routinely gap (illiquid alts, the $0.45 asset especially). `body_t = log(c/o)` captures intrabar, `r_t` captures close-to-close, but the **overnight/inter-bar gap `log(o_t/c_{t-1})` is never encoded as its own feature** — it's folded into `r_t`. For the noise-filtering payoff and for shape identity, a 5% gap-up-then-flat bar and a 5% grind-up bar are *different shapes* that may collapse to the same `r_t` bin. **Fix:** add `gap_t = log(o_t/c_{t-1})` as a feature, or make `r_t` explicitly `gap+body`. This is a real shape the candlestick literature (the proposal's own Lens 4) says is load-bearing.
- **Leak B — FAPCA "per-session re-anchoring" assumes sessions.** Crypto (the $0.45 asset is almost certainly a token) is **24/7 — there is no session boundary.** The proposal imports session re-anchoring from an equities/ABBA context (Lens 1) without checking it applies to a 64-asset mixed crypto/FX corpus. If half the assets have no sessions, "re-anchor per session" is undefined for them and drift control silently doesn't run. **Fix:** re-anchor on a fixed minute-count cadence (e.g., every 1440 min) or per-UTC-day uniformly, and state it works for 24/7 assets. Confirm which of the 64 assets even have sessions.

The core relative-transferability is otherwise correct: pooled bins + shared codebook + ratio features = structural transfer, no learned coupling. **A8's "exclude top-k mega-tokens before measuring overlap" is the single best idea in the eval** and should be elevated — the flat/doji mega-token inflating transfer overlap is exactly how a bad tokenizer fakes the central claim.

---

## (4) Cross-asset coupling — clean, but one subtle smuggle in Stage 2

Stage-1 is coupling-free (shared codebook applied per-asset independently — correct). **But Stage-2 (§2) quietly reintroduces the risk the user forbade.** A bidirectional masked-token encoder trained on the **pooled** 64-asset token stream will learn embeddings whose context windows can straddle asset boundaries if the corpus is concatenated naively, and even within-asset it learns a *single shared embedding space* across assets. That shared space is defensible (it's word-level, not cross-asset attention over price), but the proposal must **explicitly state that masking/attention never crosses an asset-sequence boundary** (no document-bleed across the concat seams) and that no positional/asset-ID conditioning is added. As written §2 doesn't say this. It's a footnote-sized fix but it's the exact place "no cross-asset coupling" gets violated by accident. *(Out of scope for the Stage-1 gate per TASK_791 line 62, but flag it now so 793 doesn't drift.)*

---

## (5) What the research missed (gaps no lens covered)

- **No null/fallback token semantics tie-back to "viable."** The spec (TASK_791 line 22) demands a defined "viable vs null" partition. The proposal defines *viable* (recurs ≥ `p_min`) but **never defines what the trader sees for a *null* run** — is it a single `<UNK>` token, dropped entirely, or coded as raw bars? §4 says "dropped from the trader's input," but A1's MDL needs them *coded*, and Stage-2 needs *something* at that position or the bar-position alignment to the trader breaks. **These two requirements conflict** (drop for the trader vs. code for MDL vs. placeholder for embedding alignment) and the proposal never reconciles them. This is an under-defined seam that will bite at integration.
- **No measurement of token *length distribution* sanity as a gate.** "Variable-length, emergent" is a spec requirement. A degenerate tokenizer can pass MDL + transfer while producing tokens that are all length-1 or one mega-length-200 token. A4 reports candles-per-token but sets **no pass band** on the *distribution*. **Fix:** add a gate that the token-length distribution is non-degenerate (e.g., median length in [3, ~30], no single token covering >X% of bars) — this is the only direct test that "variable-length shape" actually emerged.
- **Determinism of greedy longest-match decode is assumed, not gated.** §4's online path uses "greedy longest-match" against the BPE vocab, but BPE merge-order (not longest-match) is what *built* the vocab. **Greedy-longest-match ≠ BPE-merge-order tokenization** and can produce a *different* segmentation than training, breaking A0/A7 invariance silently at serving time. This is a classic BPE inference bug. **Fix:** serve with the exact BPE merge ranking, not longest-match, and add an A0-at-serving check.

---

## (6) Does the eval PROVE "the language is right"? — No, it proves "well-formed," and the proposal admits it but mis-weights

The proposal's own §3 closing caveat is honest: these gates "prove the language is well-formed, recurring, and transferable — **not** that tokens carry tradeable meaning." That's the correct scope per the SPEC (meaning is Stage 2/3). **The problem is the weighting inside that honest frame:** the verdict rule leans on A3 (circular, §1 above) and an underspecified A1 (un-evaluable, §2 above) as the two pillars. Strip those two and what *actually* survives as a real proof of "good language" is:

- **A8 cross-asset transfer with mega-tokens excluded** — this is the only gate that tests the *central product claim* and is hard to game. It should be THE headline, not A1.
- **A2 reconstruction-within-ratio-tolerance** — genuine, and reward-critical for Stage 3 (the spec calls phantom decode error → phantom alpha).
- **A1 MDL** — genuine *only after* the fallback-bit and boundary-bit fixes.

**Recommended re-weighting of the verdict rule:** Ship to Stage-2 iff **(A8 transfer at mid-frequency, mega-tokens excluded) AND (A2 fidelity) AND (A1 corrected, full-stream MDL beats a *random-merge same-size vocab*, not just raw-entropy) AND (non-degenerate length distribution)**. Drop A3-vs-shuffle. A0 stays as the cheap correctness pre-gate. This makes the gate test the *product*, not the *autocorrelation of price*.

findings.lens: Symbolic / quantized representations of time series (SAX family + ABBA + grammar induction), read specifically as a recipe for a relative-move, scale/offset-invariant, variable-length candle tokenizer whose vocabulary must be judged WITHOUT any next-bar predictor.

methods.name: SAX (Symbolic Aggregate approXimation) + PAA
methods.summary: Per-window z-normalize, reduce to w segment-means (PAA), then map each mean to a letter via fixed Gaussian breakpoints chosen so every symbol is equiprobable (equal area under N(0,1)). MINDIST letter-distance lower-bounds Euclidean.
methods.borrow: Adopt the INVARIANCE recipe but at the bar level, not the window level: SAX's per-window z-norm is exactly how it kills absolute price-level and amplitude. For us, work on log-returns r_t = log(close_t/close_{t-1}); a log-return is already offset/scale-invariant, so a token built from log-returns transfers across $225 and $0.45 assets by construction (this is the SPEC's 'x1.25' = a fixed log-return bin). Borrow the EQUIPROBABLE-BIN idea for choosing return bins: set breakpoints at empirical quantiles of the pooled 64-asset log-return distribution so each move-symbol is equally frequent (do NOT assume Gaussian — minute returns are fat-tailed; see aSAX warning). Keep MINDIST as a cheap sanity metric only.
methods.source: Lin, Keogh, Lonardi, Chiu, 'A Symbolic Representation of Time Series' (cs.ucr.edu/~eamonn/SAX.pdf); algorithm walkthrough jmotif.github.io/sax-vsm_site/morea/algorithm/SAX.html

methods.name: 1d-SAX (mean + slope per segment)
methods.summary: Augments each PAA segment with the SLOPE from a linear regression, quantizes mean and slope separately (e.g. 4x4=16 symbols), so trend within a segment is captured — SAX's known blind spot.
methods.borrow: A candle is not a scalar: it has direction AND magnitude AND a body/wick shape. 1d-SAX is the proof that you should encode at least TWO quantized channels per primitive. For us, per-bar tokenize a small tuple = (signed log-return magnitude bin, body/range bin) or (mean-move, slope) so 'up x1.25' and 'down x1.8' live on the same axis with sign. Use a product alphabet (move-level x shape-level) exactly like 1d-SAX's 4x4 grid; keep each axis's bins equiprobable.
methods.source: Malinowski, Guyet, Quiniou, Tavenard, '1d-SAX' IDA 2013 (files01.core.ac.uk/download/pdf/48197421.pdf)

methods.name: ABBA (Adaptive Brownian-Bridge-based Aggregation)
methods.summary: Two stages. COMPRESS: greedy adaptive polygonal chain — extend a linear piece while max reconstruction error <= a tolerance 'tol', emit each piece as a tuple (len, inc) = (#points, value increment). DIGITIZE: standardize len and inc each by their std, weight inc vs len by a scaling param 'scl', k-means cluster the tuples into k symbols (k auto-chooseable from a digitization tolerance). Reconstruction error modelled as a Brownian bridge, making it near parameter-free.
methods.borrow: This is the closest existing method to our SPEC. Map directly: the SPEC's '3 bars up x1.25' IS an ABBA tuple (len=3, inc=+log-move). Build the candle stream as a polygonal chain over log-close, adaptively segment by an error tolerance so segment LENGTH IS VARIABLE (solves our variable-length requirement with no fixed window), then cluster (len, inc) tuples into the alphabet. CRITICAL adaptations: (a) use inc on LOG prices so inc is a relative move -> cross-asset invariant; (b) fit the digitizer on the POOLED 64-asset tuple set so one shared codebook transfers across assets (transferability becomes a property of the shared relative encoding, exactly as SPEC demands — NOT cross-asset attention); (c) tune 'scl' so shape (inc) dominates over duration (len) if you want price-shape tokens; (d) k chosen by the no-predictor gates below, not by hand.
methods.source: Elsworth & Güttel, 'ABBA', Data Min. Knowl. Disc. 2020 (arxiv.org/abs/2003.12469); code github.com/nla-group/ABBA

methods.name: LLM-ABBA / FAPCA (symbols -> token embeddings; fixed-point drift fix)
methods.summary: Feeds ABBA symbols straight into an LLM by mapping each symbol to an existing vocabulary token, using each cluster's real-valued center as a 'natural word embedding'. Replaces ABBA's increment tuples with FIXED-POINT (length, absolute_value) anchors (FAPCA) so cumulative reconstruction drift is cancelled at piece endpoints on long sequences.
methods.borrow: This validates our exact 3-stage pipeline: (1) ABBA-style tokenizer -> (2) a model that LEARNS TOKEN EMBEDDINGS (their cluster-center-as-embedding is the seed; we replace it with a learned word2vec/masked-token embedding in stage 2) -> (3) downstream model on tokens. Two concrete borrows: (a) initialize stage-2 token embeddings from the codebook cluster centroids (len, inc) instead of random — free structure; (b) for our minute streams over long horizons, adopt FAPCA's fixed-point anchoring so token boundaries re-anchor to actual prices periodically and increment errors don't accumulate across a day.
methods.source: Carson et al., 'LLM-ABBA', 2024 (arxiv.org/html/2411.18506v2)

methods.name: Persist (Mörchen & Ultsch) — NO-PREDICTOR quality gate
methods.summary: Unsupervised discretization quality measure: for each symbol s compare its marginal P(s) to its self-transition Pr(s)=P(s_t|s_{t-1}=s) via symmetric KL, signed by sgn(Pr(s)-P(s)); score = sign * SKL(P,Q). High score = symbols PERSIST (recur in runs) => they capture real states, not noise. Greedily adds breakpoints until persistence stops increasing, auto-selecting symbol count.
methods.borrow: This is the primary no-prediction vocabulary gate the SPEC needs. A good candle language should have tokens that recur in temporally-structured runs, not flicker randomly. Compute Persist over the token stream: if shuffling the stream destroys the score (high SKL on real, ~0 on shuffled) the vocabulary has captured genuine temporal structure WITHOUT forecasting anything. Also reuse Persist's greedy stop-criterion to pick alphabet/k. This directly replaces the wrong 'predict next-bar sign' gate.
methods.source: Mörchen & Ultsch, 'Finding Persisting States...' / 'Optimizing time series discretization', and Cornanguer et al. 2023 restatement (arxiv.org/html/2301.05041)

methods.name: MDL intrinsic cardinality/dimensionality (Hu, Rakthanmanon, Keogh)
methods.summary: Uses Minimum Description Length to pick the discretization CARDINALITY (alphabet size) and number of segments with no task/label: minimize total bits = bits to store the discretized model + bits to store the residual (reconstruction error). MDL recovered the correct cardinality (=10) on controlled data.
methods.borrow: Second no-predictor gate and the principled way to set alphabet size k and segmentation granularity. Score a candidate tokenizer by description length: bits(codebook) + bits(token sequence) + bits(residual candles given tokens). The k / tolerance that minimizes total bits is the right vocabulary size — over-large alphabets are penalized by model bits, over-coarse ones by residual bits. This makes 'is the vocabulary good?' a measurable compression question, no forecast involved.
methods.source: Hu, Rakthanmanon, Hao, Evans, Lonardi, Keogh, 'intrinsic cardinality and dimensionality via MDL', DMKD 2014 (link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s10618-014-0345-2)

methods.name: SFA (Symbolic Fourier Approximation) + MCB
methods.summary: DFT each window, keep the lowest/highest-variance Fourier coefficients, then quantize each coefficient with data-adaptive bins learned from the coefficient's empirical distribution (Multiple Coefficient Binning) rather than fixed Gaussian breakpoints. Better noise robustness and approximation than SAX.
methods.borrow: Take MCB's lesson, not the Fourier transform (DFT smears our sharp minute candles). MCB = learn breakpoints PER CHANNEL from the actual data distribution. Apply it to our per-bar channels (return magnitude, body, wick) and to ABBA's (len, inc) dimensions: fit each dimension's bins on the pooled corpus so bins are informative for fat-tailed minute returns. This is the data-adaptive-breakpoint principle that fixes SAX's Gaussian assumption.
methods.source: Schäfer & Högqvist, 'SFA', EDBT 2012 (www2.informatik.hu-berlin.de/~schaefpa/sfa_trie.pdf); pyts SFA docs

methods.name: SAX + Sequitur grammar induction (GrammarViz)
methods.summary: After SAX-discretizing into a symbol string, run Sequitur to induce a context-free grammar; its non-terminal rules ARE recurring variable-length subsequences (motifs). 'Numerosity reduction' (collapsing consecutive identical words) is what enables discovering patterns of different lengths.
methods.borrow: This is how a TOKEN (variable-length recurring shape, e.g. the whole SPEC string '3 up x1.25, down x1.8, ...') emerges from a per-bar symbol alphabet WITHOUT predicting. Pipeline for us: per-bar move-symbols (from SAX/MCB bins) -> Sequitur/BPE-style grammar over the symbol stream -> each frequent rule becomes a candle TOKEN. Borrow 'numerosity reduction' as the SPEC's noise filter: bar-runs that don't compress into a recurring rule are exactly the noise the trader should IGNORE. Grammar coverage (% of stream explained by reusable rules) is a third no-predictor quality metric. (BPE is the modern, simpler swap for Sequitur and gives byte-pair token merges directly.)
methods.source: Senin, Lin, et al., 'GrammarViz 2.0/3.0' (csdl.ics.hawaii.edu/techreports/2017/17-04/17-04.pdf); Senin 'grammar-based compression' EDBT 2015

key_takeaways: Our SPEC token = an ABBA (len, inc) tuple stream where 'inc' is a LOG-return (relative move). ABBA already does adaptive variable-length segmentation + clustering into an alphabet; it is the closest off-the-shelf scaffold and should be the starting design.

Scale/offset invariance is achieved structurally, not learned: SAX gets it by per-window z-norm; we get it more cheaply by encoding on log-returns/ratios so 'x1.25' is the same symbol at $225 and $0.45. Cross-asset transfer then follows from a SHARED codebook fit on the pooled 64-asset return distribution — never from cross-asset attention.

There are at least three legitimate NO-PREDICTOR vocabulary-quality gates, all grounded: (1) Persist self-transition KL (tokens should recur in runs, beat a shuffled baseline), (2) MDL total description length (model+residual bits) to pick alphabet size k, (3) reconstruction error of the original candles from tokens (ABBA/LLM-ABBA's standard metric). None forecasts anything.
Two quantized channels per primitive beat one (1d-SAX): encode at least magnitude AND shape/slope per bar; use a product alphabet of equiprobable bins per channel.

Variable-length recurring tokens emerge by grammar induction / BPE over a per-bar symbol stream (GrammarViz/Sequitur). 'Numerosity reduction' IS the SPEC's promised noise filter: non-compressible bar-runs are dropped, giving the denoised compressed stream the trader consumes.
Bin breakpoints must be data-adaptive (SFA/MCB, aSAX), NOT fixed Gaussian — minute log-returns are fat-tailed and near-zero-centered, so Gaussian equiprobable bins will mis-bin the tails that matter.
directly_applicable: ABBA compression: greedily extend a linear piece over the log-close polygonal chain while reconstruction error <= tol; emit (len, inc) per piece -> gives variable-length segments with one tolerance knob (SPEC's variable-length requirement, solved).
Encode 'inc' as a log-return so the move is a ratio: log(1.25)=+0.223 is one symbol regardless of price level -> SPEC's cross-asset $225 vs $0.45 example maps to the identical token.
Fit the (len, inc) k-means digitizer / the per-channel quantile bins ONCE on the pooled 64-asset corpus -> a single shared codebook = transferability as a property of the encoding.
Use 1d-SAX-style product alphabet: quantize signed-move-magnitude x body/slope into a small grid per bar (e.g. 8 x 4) with equiprobable (quantile) bins per axis.
Run BPE / Sequitur over the per-bar symbol stream; frequent merge rules = the variable-length candle TOKENS (the full SPEC string '3 up x1.25, down x1.8, 1.4, 1.2, 1.2, up x1.85' is one such rule).

Vocabulary-good gate, no predictor: (a) Persist KL score on token stream vs shuffled control; (b) MDL bits sweep over k to pick alphabet size; (c) candle reconstruction MSE from tokens vs compression ratio curve; (d) grammar/BPE coverage of the stream.
Adopt ABBA 'scl' to bias clustering toward shape over duration, and FAPCA fixed-point re-anchoring per session so increment errors don't drift across a trading day.
Initialize stage-2 token embeddings from the codebook centroids (LLM-ABBA cluster-center-as-embedding) before word2vec/masked-token training.
warnings: Do NOT use SAX's fixed Gaussian breakpoints on minute returns: aSAX/SFA/empirical studies show real series violate Gaussianity; fat-tailed near-zero minute log-returns will collapse most bars into the middle symbol and under-resolve the large moves that matter. Use empirical-quantile / MCB / k-means breakpoints.

SAX per-window z-norm has a documented pathology on near-flat windows: a tiny move in an otherwise constant window gets amplified to a huge z-score. Minute candles have many quiet stretches; guard with a min-std floor (don't normalize below threshold) or avoid window z-norm entirely by using log-returns.

ABBA increment encoding accumulates reconstruction drift over long sequences (the reason LLM-ABBA introduced FAPCA fixed points). For multi-hour minute streams, re-anchor to absolute price periodically or token boundaries will slide off real candles.

Reconstruction error ALONE is a deceptive quality gate: it monotonically improves with more symbols/segments (negative correlation reconstruction-error vs #partitions is documented). Always pair it with MDL (which penalizes alphabet bloat) or you'll just pick the largest vocabulary.

Persist's standard form scores a single 1-D quantization; our tokens are multi-channel/variable-length, so Persist must be computed on the final token-ID stream (and ideally compared to a time-shuffled baseline), not on a raw single channel, or the score won't reflect token quality.
Don't pull in SFA's DFT itself: Fourier bases smear sharp single-bar spikes and wick structure that are informative in candles. Borrow only MCB's data-adaptive binning, not the frequency transform.

k-means on (len, inc) is scale-sensitive; without ABBA's per-dimension standardization + 'scl', segment LENGTH (large integers) will dominate INCREMENT and your tokens will cluster by duration instead of by price-shape — the opposite of what the SPEC wants.

Grammar induction quality depends entirely on the base alphabet: too coarse and no motifs recur; too fine and identical shapes split across symbols so no rule reaches frequency threshold. The alphabet-size gates (MDL/Persist) must be set BEFORE judging grammar coverage.

findings.lens: Discovering recurring, variable-length subsequences as a vocabulary of price-action "shapes" (our tokens). Two classical families are directly relevant: (A) Matrix-Profile / motif discovery (STAMP, STOMP, SCRIMP, VALMOD, uniform-scaling motifs) — finds recurring subsequences geometrically via z-normalized distance; (B) Symbolic grammar induction (SAX -> Sequitur/RePair, GrammarViz) and BPE-over-symbols — discretizes first, then builds a HIERARCHICAL, variable-length VOCABULARY of recurring strings, which is the closest existing analog to "a language of shapes." The discretize-then-merge pipeline (SAX + grammar/BPE) is the spine of our tokenizer; Matrix-Profile gives the geometric "is-this-shape-actually-recurring" validator that has no symbolization artifacts. Crucially, every method here is descriptive/compressive, NOT predictive — they discover what recurs, never forecast — which matches our hard "no prediction" constraint. Vocabulary quality is judged with intrinsic, label-free metrics (compression ratio, grammar/token coverage, rule-density, Zipfian/entropy of token frequencies), giving us a no-downstream-predictor gate.

methods.name: SAX discretization + numerosity reduction (the variable-length enabler)
methods.summary: SAX z-normalizes a sliding window, reduces it via PAA (averaging W-length segments), then bins each segment into an alphabet letter (equiprobable Gaussian breakpoints) to make a 'word'. Numerosity reduction then collapses consecutive identical SAX words, keeping only the first occurrence + its start position.
methods.borrow: Use SAX-style discretization as our Stage-1 symbol layer BUT over RELATIVE moves, not raw price: z-normalize/PAA a window of bar-to-bar log-returns (or the AR delta variation below), then bin. Numerosity reduction is the key trick we should copy: collapsing repeated identical symbols is precisely what makes downstream merges produce VARIABLE-LENGTH tokens (a flat run of 8 bars and 12 bars both reduce to the same symbol, so the same token can span different bar counts). It also kills the 'trivial match' explosion from overlapping windows.
methods.source: Senin et al., GrammarViz 3.0 (ACM TKDD 2018), osti.gov/pages/servlets/purl/1432619 §3.2; Lin et al. SAX (2002)

methods.name: Sequitur / RePair grammar induction -> hierarchical recurring-pattern vocabulary
methods.summary: Sequitur reads the symbol string and forms a context-free grammar under two constraints: digram uniqueness (no pair of adjacent symbols repeats without being a rule) and rule utility (every rule/non-terminal is used >=2 times, i.e. it MUST be recurring). Each non-terminal is a recurring sub-pattern; nesting (R4->R3 bac, R3->R1 R2) builds longer patterns from shorter ones. RePair is the offline, frequency-greedy variant (repeatedly replace the most frequent digram) that GrammarViz found gives cleaner motifs.
methods.borrow: This is the cleanest blueprint for 'a language of shapes': the grammar's non-terminals ARE our token vocabulary, and the rule-utility constraint gives us a built-in definition of a 'viable' token = one that recurs >=2x. The hierarchy (rules built from rules) means we get short tokens AND long composite tokens for free, exactly the variable-length structure we want. Prefer the RePair/offline-greedy flavor — it is essentially BPE and is the most controllable.
methods.source: Nevill-Manning & Witten, Sequitur; Larsson & Moffat, RE-PAIR; Senin et al. GrammarViz 3.0 §3.3

methods.name: BPE over discretized series (Tavabi & Lerman) — incl. the Autoregressive/delta variation
methods.summary: Normalize -> PAA -> bin to K symbols, then run text-style BPE: each iteration find the most frequent adjacent symbol pair across ALL series and merge it into a new symbol; iterate. They run BPE separately on several 'variations' of the symbol stream and merge results: RCS (drop all repeats), RCSM (median-length repeat), and crucially an AUTOREGRESSIVE variation y_t = x_t - x_{t-1} that encodes the SLOPE/step between bins rather than the level.
methods.borrow: Two things. (1) BPE-merge is our token-builder; it is identical in spirit to RePair but trivially implementable and the vocabulary is SHARED across all 64 assets by construction (merge counts pooled over every asset), which is exactly how we get cross-asset token transfer WITHOUT cross-asset attention. (2) The AR/delta variation is the concrete recipe for our relative-shape requirement: symbolize the DIFFERENCES (or ratios) between consecutive bars, so a token is defined by relative moves and is automatically invariant to absolute price level — '$225 vs $0.45' collapse to the same token because only the step pattern is encoded.
methods.source: Tavabi & Lerman, 'Pattern Discovery in Time Series with Byte Pair Encoding', arXiv:2106.00614 §3.1-3.5

methods.name: Pattern-centric BPE tokenizer for foundation models (Götz et al. 2025)
methods.summary: Modern, scaled version of the above built explicitly as a TOKENIZER. z-normalize, quantize into M equiprobable/uniform bins over +-5 sigma, run BPE merges until new tokens occur less than p_min times. They build ONE shared vocabulary on 100M samples; tune M (22/37/126 bins -> ~1.4-2.4k tokens, 2-4x compression). 'Conditional decoding' learns context-dependent bin centers (M^2 params, no gradients) to undo quantization error. Flat runs compress automatically because identical adjacent symbols merge.
methods.borrow: This is our exact architecture target and validates the whole approach (it gave 1990% efficiency gain from token compression — our stated payoff). Borrow concretely: (a) the p_min frequency stopping rule for BPE (stop merging when a candidate token appears < p_min times across the corpus — this is our 'viable token' threshold); (b) build ONE shared vocabulary across all 64 assets, applied zero-shot to unseen assets; (c) sweep bin count M as the main knob trading vocabulary granularity vs compression. Ignore their forecasting head — we only take the tokenizer half, which is prediction-free.
methods.source: Götz, Kollovieh, Günnemann, Schwinn, 'Byte Pair Encoding for Efficient Time Series Forecasting', arXiv:2505.14411

methods.name: Matrix Profile (STAMP / STOMP / SCRIMP++)
methods.summary: For a fixed window length m, compute every subsequence's z-normalized Euclidean distance to its nearest non-trivial neighbor (via the MASS/FFT trick). The 'matrix profile' is that nearest-neighbor distance curve; its lowest points are motifs (most-recurring shapes), highest are discords (anomalies). STAMP (random order), STOMP (ordered, O(n^2) but ~log n faster constant), SCRIMP++ (anytime, fast approximate-then-exact).
methods.borrow: Use Matrix Profile as the SYMBOLIZATION-FREE ground truth for 'does this shape genuinely recur?'. After BPE/grammar proposes a token, take its occurrences and confirm they are tight under z-normalized Euclidean distance on the raw relative-move window — this catches tokens that are merge artifacts of the binning rather than real recurring shapes. The z-normalization built into the matrix profile is exactly our location+scale invariance (level and amplitude removed). It is a validator, not the tokenizer (fixed m, geometric, no vocabulary).
methods.source: Yeh et al. Matrix Profile I/II; Zhu et al. STOMP; Zhu et al. SCRIMP++; UCR Matrix Profile page cs.ucr.edu/~eamonn/MatrixProfile.html

methods.name: VALMOD — variable-length motif discovery
methods.summary: Removes the fixed-window assumption of Matrix Profile: computes matrix profiles for a RANGE [l_min, l_max] of window lengths at once using a novel lower bound (it cheaply bounds longer-length distances from a computed shorter length), and returns for each position the best length. Reports a LENGTH-NORMALIZED distance so motifs of different lengths are comparable (longer motifs aren't unfairly penalized).
methods.borrow: Adopt the length-normalized distance idea so our variable-length tokens can be compared/ranked on equal footing (divide z-normalized Euclidean distance by sqrt(length)). Use VALMOD over a bar-length range (e.g. l_min=4 .. l_max=64 bars) as an independent, vocabulary-free census of what variable-length shapes actually recur in our 64-asset minute data — a sanity check that the BPE token-length distribution matches where real recurring structure lives.
methods.source: Linardi, Zhu, Palpanas, Keogh, 'Matrix Profile X: VALMOD', SIGMOD 2018; financial application iccs-meeting.org/archive/iccs2019/papers/115400736.pdf

methods.name: Uniform-scaling motif matching (time-axis invariance)
methods.summary: z-normalization removes amplitude (price-level/scale) differences but NOT time-axis stretching: a 10-bar shape and the 'same' shape drawn out over 15 bars stay misaligned after z-norm. Uniform scaling stretches/compresses one subsequence to a common reference length over a small scaling-factor range, then compares with Euclidean distance, so the same morphology matches regardless of how many bars it spans.
methods.borrow: This formalizes WHY our token must be defined by relative shape, not bar count, and gives a fallback if pure SAX numerosity reduction doesn't fully absorb tempo differences: allow a token to match occurrences at a small set of time-scalings (e.g. +-20% bar count) when clustering occurrences/validating. Pairs naturally with the relative-move encoding: relative moves give price-scale invariance, uniform scaling gives time-scale invariance — together = the full level/scale/position/location invariance our spec demands.
methods.source: Yankov, Keogh, Medina, Chiu, Zordan, 'Detecting Time Series Motifs Under Uniform Scaling', KDD 2007, cs.ucr.edu/~eamonn/motifs_under_scaling.pdf

methods.name: GrammarViz rule pruning: clustering + greedy minimum-cardinality maximum-cover
methods.summary: Raw Sequitur/RePair produces FAR too many rules (e.g. 252) with heavy overlap. GrammarViz prunes in two stages: (1) pool all subsequences a rule expands to, drop overlapping ones, hierarchically cluster the remaining similar-length subsequences -> each cluster = one motif (252 -> 25); (2) 'grammar cover' = fraction of the series covered by chosen rules; a greedy minimum-cardinality set-cover keeps the smallest rule set that still covers most of the series.
methods.borrow: This is our vocabulary-pruning recipe to get from raw BPE merges to a clean, non-redundant token set. (a) Cluster near-duplicate tokens (tokens whose occurrence-subsequences are within a small z-normalized distance) and keep one canonical token per cluster — collapses synonyms. (b) Use greedy set-cover on 'fraction of the candle stream explained' to pick the SMALLEST vocabulary that still covers most bars — directly operationalizes 'keep only viable tokens, let the trader ignore non-token noise runs'. The uncovered residual IS our noise filter.
methods.source: Senin et al., GrammarViz 3.0 §5 (Heuristic 1 clustering, Heuristic 2 grammar-cover set-cover)

methods.name: Rule-density / grammar-cover curve (label-free structure score)
methods.summary: GrammarViz builds a per-timepoint 'rule density' array: for every grammar rule, increment a counter on every time-point its occurrences span. High density = heavily-reused (compressible/normal) structure; global minima = points no rule covers = anomalies/noise. Grounded in Kolmogorov-complexity / MDL: a good grammar maximally compresses the string.
methods.borrow: Two uses with NO predictor. (1) As a vocabulary-quality score: a good token language should give HIGH average coverage / rule-density over held-out asset streams — most bars belong to some recurring token. (2) As the runtime noise gate the spec wants: bars sitting in rule-density minima are exactly the 'candle runs that don't map to a viable token' the trader should ignore. Track coverage on held-out assets to confirm cross-asset transfer of the vocabulary.
methods.source: Senin et al., GrammarViz 3.0 §4 (rule density curve, Kolmogorov/MDL framing)

methods.name: Intrinsic, label-free tokenizer-quality metrics (the no-predictor gate)
methods.summary: From NLP/time-series tokenizer evaluation: judge a vocabulary WITHOUT any downstream task via compression ratio (mean tokens per input unit; lower=better), fertility, Rényi/Shannon entropy of the token-frequency distribution and Zipfian fit (natural vocabularies are power-law), token-space UTILIZATION (Cramér's V — how evenly tokens are used; many dead/rarely-used tokens = bad), and fraction of unused tokens. Compression correlates with downstream quality but does not perfectly predict it.
methods.borrow: This is our replacement for the discarded next-bar-sign probe. Define the Stage-1 'is the language good?' gate as a panel of intrinsic metrics computed on HELD-OUT assets: (1) compression ratio of the candle stream; (2) bar-coverage / grammar-cover (above); (3) cross-asset vocabulary overlap — fraction of tokens that fire on multiple assets (directly measures the transfer property); (4) token-frequency entropy / Zipfian fit (a healthy language is power-law, not one mega-token + dead tail); (5) % near-dead tokens (prune target). None of these require predicting anything.
methods.source: EmergentMind 'Intrinsic Tokenizer Metrics'; Goldman et al. arXiv:2403.06265; 'Small Vocabularies, Big Gains' arXiv:2511.11622 (Cramér's V token-space utilization)

key_takeaways: The dominant, proven recipe is DISCRETIZE-THEN-MERGE: SAX-style symbolization (with numerosity reduction) followed by a frequency-greedy merge (BPE == RePair). This is literally a hierarchical vocabulary of recurring variable-length patterns — the closest existing analog to our 'language of shapes' — and it is descriptive, never predictive.

Variable length comes from TWO complementary mechanisms, use both: (a) numerosity reduction collapses repeated symbols so a token can span different bar counts; (b) hierarchical merging (BPE/grammar) composes short tokens into longer ones. A token's bar-length is emergent, not a hyperparameter.

Our two hard invariances map cleanly onto known tricks: PRICE-scale/level invariance = encode RELATIVE moves (log-returns / the AR-delta variation) + z-normalization; TIME-scale invariance = numerosity reduction (+ uniform-scaling matching as backstop). Cross-asset transfer is free if the merge statistics are POOLED across all 64 assets into ONE shared vocabulary — exactly our 'property of relative encoding, not learned attention' claim.

Vocabulary pruning to 'viable' tokens is a SOLVED problem with three ingredients we can lift directly: a frequency floor p_min as the merge stopping rule, near-duplicate clustering to remove synonym tokens, and greedy set-cover to keep the smallest vocabulary that still covers most bars. The uncovered residual is our built-in noise filter.

We can fully judge vocabulary quality with NO predictor: compression ratio, bar/grammar coverage on held-out assets, cross-asset token overlap, token-frequency entropy/Zipfian fit, and dead-token fraction. Matrix Profile / VALMOD give an independent, symbolization-free census of what truly recurs to cross-check that BPE tokens are real shapes, not binning artifacts.
directly_applicable: Symbol layer = SAX-style: z-normalize + PAA a sliding window of RELATIVE moves (log-returns / consecutive ratios), bin to K letters (equiprobable). Then apply numerosity reduction (collapse consecutive identical words, keep first + position).
Token builder = BPE / RePair merge loop with merge counts POOLED across all 64 assets into a single shared vocabulary (gives cross-asset transfer by construction).
Use the AR/delta variation (y_t = x_t - x_{t-1} over bins) to encode slope/relative step, making tokens invariant to absolute price level ($225 vs $0.45 collapse).

Merge-stopping rule = p_min frequency floor (token must recur >= p_min times across corpus to be admitted) — this is the operational definition of a 'viable' token; equivalently Sequitur's rule-utility (>=2 occurrences) constraint.

Vocabulary cleanup = (1) cluster near-duplicate tokens by z-normalized distance on their occurrence-windows, keep one canonical per cluster; (2) greedy minimum-cardinality set-cover to keep the smallest token set covering most bars.

No-predictor quality gate = panel of intrinsic metrics on HELD-OUT assets: compression ratio, bar-coverage (grammar-cover), cross-asset token-overlap %, token-frequency entropy/Zipfian fit, % dead tokens.

Independent validator = Matrix Profile (fixed lengths) + VALMOD (length range l_min..l_max bars, length-normalized distance) to confirm proposed tokens correspond to genuinely recurring z-normalized shapes; runtime noise filter = rule-density / coverage minima -> bars the trader ignores.
Tunable knobs to sweep, in priority: K (bin count / symbol granularity), p_min (merge floor / vocabulary size), PAA window W, and motif length range for the VALMOD cross-check.
warnings: Discretization is lossy and merge artifacts are real: BPE/grammar can mint a 'token' that is just a frequent binning coincidence, not a recurring shape. Always validate proposed tokens against the symbolization-FREE Matrix-Profile/z-normalized distance before admitting them. Götz et al. needed 'conditional decoding' specifically to repair quantization error.

Bin-boundary brittleness: a near-threshold relative move can fall in different bins on two assets, so the 'same' shape yields different symbol strings and fails to merge into the same token. Mitigate with overlapping/soft bins, numerosity reduction, and the cluster-near-duplicates step; do NOT rely on exact-string equality alone.

Numerosity reduction discards repeat COUNTS (8 flat bars vs 12 flat bars become identical). For trading, run-length can matter; Tavabi's RCSM (median-length) and AR variations exist precisely because pure RCS loses information — keep at least one run-length-aware variation rather than collapsing blindly.

Vocabulary explosion + Zipfian tail: raw Sequitur produced 252 rules pruned to 25; expect a huge dead tail of near-unique tokens. Without aggressive p_min + set-cover pruning the 'language' is mostly noise and the compression payoff evaporates.

Intrinsic metrics are necessary, not sufficient: the tokenizer-eval literature warns compression/entropy correlate with but do NOT perfectly predict downstream usefulness. Treat the no-predictor panel as a GATE to reject bad vocabularies, not a guarantee of a good one — but per our spec, fixing Stage-1 language quality first is exactly the right scope.

These classical methods are univariate-per-asset and assume reasonably clean series; minute OHLC has gaps, halts, and microstructure noise. SAX/PAA smoothing helps, but flat/illiquid runs will dominate token frequencies unless explicitly handled (they auto-compress to one mega-token, skewing the vocabulary).

VALMOD/Matrix Profile are O(n^2)-ish; on 64 assets x minute granularity over long history they are a validation/offline tool, not something to run in the trading loop. Budget them as periodic audits, with BPE tokenization as the cheap online path.

findings.lens: LEARNED discrete tokenizers for time series + the self-supervised "token embedding" (token-meaning) stage, evaluated strictly under our constraints: ONE-asset minute-candle streams, RELATIVE/scale-invariant encoding, NO forecasting anywhere, and a vocabulary that must be judged GOOD intrinsically (no downstream predictor). Cross-asset transfer must fall out of the relative encoding, not learned cross-asset attention.

methods.name: TOTEM (VQ-VAE time-series tokenizer)
methods.summary: Per-channel (univariate) 1D-conv VQ-VAE that self-supervisedly tokenizes a single time-series stream into discrete codewords via reconstruction + commitment loss only. Concrete config: codebook K=256 codewords, code dim D=64, temporal compression factor F=4 (each token summarizes ~4 time steps), commitment cost 0.25, 2 residual layers. Reconstruction performance plateaus K=256 vs 512.
methods.borrow: This is our closest skeleton for a LEARNED tokenizer: a 1D-conv encoder over ONE asset's candle stream -> VQ codebook -> 1D-conv decoder, trained ONLY to reconstruct (no prediction). Adopt its exact non-predictive training recipe and start near K=256/D=64. Critically, TOTEM operates per-channel independently, which is exactly how cross-asset transfer should arise in our system: the SAME codebook is applied to every asset, so a relative shape recurring on a $225 asset and a $0.45 asset hits the same code WITHOUT any cross-asset attention. Caveat: TOTEM's F=4 is a FIXED compression (fixed-length tokens), so it does not by itself give our variable-length tokens — pair with BPE-merge or dynamic patching below.
methods.source: Talukder et al., TOTEM, arXiv:2402.16412 ; config from openreview.net/pdf?id=jzIdR2TXlK

methods.name: FSQ — Finite Scalar Quantization
methods.summary: Replaces the learned VQ codebook with projecting the latent to a few (<~10) dims, each rounded to a small fixed set of levels; the implicit codebook is the product of levels. Uses bounding+rounding with straight-through estimator. No commitment loss, no codebook reseeding, no entropy penalty — and provably does NOT suffer codebook collapse.
methods.borrow: Strongly consider FSQ as the quantizer instead of vanilla VQ to sidestep codebook-collapse entirely — collapse is THE failure mode that would silently shrink our vocabulary to a handful of useless tokens. FSQ gives a fully-utilized, fixed, deterministic codebook with near-zero tuning, which also makes the vocabulary stable/reproducible across assets (a property we want: same shape -> same token, every run). Choose levels to hit a target vocab size (e.g. 8x8x8x5 ~ 2560 codes).
methods.source: Mentzer et al., 'Finite Scalar Quantization: VQ-VAE Made Simple', arXiv:2309.15505 (ICLR 2024)

methods.name: BPE for time series (Byte-Pair Encoding tokenization)
methods.summary: Discretize raw values into base symbols, then run standard BPE: iteratively merge the most frequent adjacent symbol pairs into new composite, VARIABLE-LENGTH tokens. The vocabulary is built unsupervised on frequency statistics ALONE, fully decoupled from any forecasting objective; the same vocabulary is reused across scenarios.
methods.borrow: This is the cleanest match to our 'a token = a recurring VARIABLE-LENGTH sequence of shapes' requirement, and it is intrinsically non-predictive (built from co-occurrence frequency, not labels). Recipe for us: (1) quantize each candle's RELATIVE move (ratio bins, e.g. log-return / range buckets) into base symbols -> level/scale invariant by construction; (2) run BPE over the per-asset symbol streams POOLED across all 64 assets so frequent relative-shape runs ('3 bars up x1.25, 1 down x1.8...') become single multi-bar tokens; (3) cap vocab via merge count. Frequent noise that never recurs simply never gets merged -> natural noise filtering, exactly the efficiency payoff we want.
methods.source: Götz et al., 'Byte Pair Encoding for Efficient Time Series Forecasting', arXiv:2505.14411

methods.name: SAX / PAA symbolic discretization (relative-move base alphabet)
methods.summary: Classic unsupervised mapping of a series to symbols: z-normalize a window, PAA-average into segments, map segment means to symbols via equiprobable breakpoints of a Gaussian. Standard substrate for motif discovery (recurring variable-length patterns) over a sliding window.
methods.borrow: Use SAX-style equiprobable breakpoints to build the BASE symbol alphabet that BPE then merges on — equiprobable bins guarantee balanced symbol usage (a poor-man's collapse-avoidance for the base layer). For us the discretized quantity must be the RELATIVE move (per-bar ratio / log-return, plus a coarse body-vs-wick shape code), NOT absolute price, which directly gives the price-level/scale invariance our spec demands. SAX also gives a cheap, deterministic, fully-interpretable baseline tokenizer to sanity-check the learned one against.
methods.source: Lin et al., 'Experiencing SAX', DAMI ; cs.gmu.edu/~jessica/SAX_DAMI_preprint.pdf

methods.name: TimeMAE — masked codeword classification (Stage-2 embedding model)
methods.summary: Self-supervised representation learner over time series with TWO non-forecasting objectives: (a) masked codeword classification — discretize non-overlapping sub-series into codewords via a learned tokenizer, mask some, and CLASSIFY which codeword was masked from bidirectional context; (b) masked representation regression against a momentum/target encoder. Neither objective predicts future values.
methods.borrow: This is the exact template for our Stage-2 'token embedding' model: take our token sequence, mask random tokens, and train a bidirectional encoder to recover the masked token's identity (BERT/word2vec-style cloze, NOT next-token forecasting). The encoder's hidden states become the contextual token embeddings ('meaning') we hand to the trader. The momentum-regression branch is an optional add-on to stabilize embeddings. Use TimeMAE to justify a masked-token, no-prediction Stage-2 to anyone who pushes back.
methods.source: Cheng et al., 'TimeMAE', arXiv:2303.00320 (WSDM)

methods.name: RevIN — reversible instance normalization (invariance layer)
methods.summary: Per-instance normalize (subtract mean, divide std, learnable affine) at input and symmetrically de-normalize at output, removing non-stationary mean/variance shifts without destroying them.
methods.borrow: Apply instance-normalization PER WINDOW before tokenizing so the tokenizer sees scale/level-free shape, reinforcing our relative-encoding invariance even inside a learned-VQ path (TOTEM itself does NOT normalize, which is a gap for us). For a pure relative-ratio encoding the mean/scale are already removed, so the 'reversible/de-norm' half is unneeded — we only borrow the NORMALIZE half. Treat RevIN as conceptual backing for 'strip level & scale before building the vocabulary'.
methods.source: Kim et al., 'Reversible Instance Normalization', ICLR 2022, openreview cGDAkQo1C0p

methods.name: LFQ (MAGVIT-v2) — lookup-free quantization with entropy penalty
methods.summary: Drops codebook embedding dim to zero; each latent dim is independently binarized so the codebook is implicit, enabling very LARGE vocabularies. Adds an entropy loss to force broad code utilization plus a commitment term.
methods.borrow: If we want a large vocabulary (thousands of token shapes) from the LEARNED path, LFQ scales further than VQ while staying collapse-resistant. Most transferable single idea: the entropy-of-code-usage loss — maximize batch-marginal code entropy while minimizing per-sample code entropy — which we can bolt onto ANY learned tokenizer to keep the vocabulary broad and balanced. Probably overkill vs FSQ/BPE for a first pass; keep as a scaling lever.
methods.source: Yu et al., 'Language Model Beats Diffusion: Tokenizer is Key to Visual Generation' (MAGVIT-v2/LFQ), arXiv:2310.05737 (ICLR 2024)

methods.name: TS2Vec — hierarchical contrastive timestamp representations
methods.summary: Self-supervised, non-predictive: contrastive learning at both instance and temporal levels over augmented context views (random cropping + timestamp masking), enforcing contextual consistency across multi-scale granularities.
methods.borrow: Two uses: (1) an OPTIONAL contrastive auxiliary for Stage-2 — pull together two augmented views of the same token-in-context, push apart others — to sharpen token 'meaning' without any forecasting; (2) more importantly, its evaluation philosophy: judge representations by clustering/retrieval quality, not prediction. Borrow its augmentation set (cropping, masking) as the positive-pair generator for our token-embedding contrastive option.
methods.source: Yue et al., 'TS2Vec', AAAI 2022, arXiv:2106.10466

methods.name: Intrinsic codebook/vocabulary quality metrics (NO downstream task)
methods.summary: Standard tokenizer-quality metrics that need no predictor: codebook PERPLEXITY / utilization rate (fraction of codes actually used, ideally ->100%), reconstruction error (MSE/PSNR of decode-back), average pairwise code distance (diversity), and information-theoretic measures (mutual information / token-level recoverability) as task-agnostic semantic-preservation proxies. FVQ/VQGAN-scaling lines report 99-100% utilization on 16k-262k codebooks.
methods.borrow: This is our answer to 'how do we judge the vocabulary is GOOD with NO predictor', replacing the rejected next-bar-sign probe. Build a vocabulary scorecard: (1) codebook utilization / perplexity — are most tokens used, no collapse; (2) reconstruction fidelity — can we decode tokens back to the candle shape (relative MSE); (3) usage-distribution health — Zipfian but not degenerate, low dead-token rate; (4) CROSS-ASSET coverage/stability — does the SAME token fire on multiple assets at different price levels (direct test of our invariance claim); (5) MI between token id and held-out context / compression ratio (bits-per-bar) as a language-richness proxy. All computable with zero forecasting.
methods.source: FVQ 'Scalable Training for VQ Networks with 100% Codebook Utilization' arXiv:2509.10140 ; VQGAN-100k arXiv:2406.11837 ; COSMIC MI arXiv:2402.19457

key_takeaways: Two viable tokenizer families fit our spec, and they are complementary: (A) LEARNED VQ-VAE (TOTEM skeleton) gives data-adaptive shape codes but fixed-length tokens; (B) symbolic+BPE (SAX base alphabet -> BPE merges) gives VARIABLE-LENGTH tokens and is the most literal match to our 'recurring variable-length shape' definition. Strongest first build: relative-ratio discretization (SAX-style equiprobable bins on per-bar log-returns) -> BPE merges pooled across all 64 assets. It is unsupervised, variable-length, scale-invariant, and non-predictive by construction.

Cross-asset transfer must come from the RELATIVE encoding + a SINGLE shared codebook applied per-asset, exactly as TOTEM applies one codebook per channel. No method here needs cross-asset attention to transfer — confirming our architectural stance. The test that it worked is intrinsic: the same token id fires on multiple assets at wildly different price levels.

Codebook collapse is the dominant failure mode of any LEARNED tokenizer and would silently destroy the vocabulary. Pick a collapse-immune quantizer up front: FSQ (simplest, no aux losses, no collapse) or LFQ+entropy-loss (for large vocab). If using plain VQ, you MUST add EMA updates + dead-code reset + usage-entropy penalty.

Stage-2 (token meaning) is a SOLVED template under our no-forecasting rule: TimeMAE's masked-codeword-classification = BERT/word2vec cloze over token sequences -> contextual token embeddings, with an optional TS2Vec-style contrastive auxiliary. Explicitly avoid next-token-prediction framing; use masked-token RECOVERY instead.

We can judge vocabulary quality with NO predictor via a four-part intrinsic scorecard: codebook utilization/perplexity, reconstruction fidelity, usage-distribution health (Zipfian, low dead-token rate), and cross-asset token coverage/stability. This directly replaces the discarded next-bar-sign gate.
directly_applicable: Relative-move base discretization: encode each candle by its RATIO move (log-return + range/body/wick ratios) into SAX-style equiprobable bins -> guarantees price-level/scale/position invariance and balanced base-symbol usage.

BPE merge layer over the pooled-across-64-assets symbol stream -> variable-length tokens where frequent multi-bar shapes become one token; non-recurring noise never merges (built-in denoising / the efficiency payoff in our spec).
Single shared codebook applied per-asset (TOTEM per-channel pattern) -> cross-asset transfer with zero cross-asset attention.
FSQ as the quantizer if we take the learned-VQ route -> eliminates codebook collapse with no aux-loss tuning; sets a deterministic, reproducible vocabulary.
