Per-window instance normalization (RevIN 'normalize' half) before any learned encoder -> reinforces invariance for the VQ path.
Stage-2 = masked-token recovery (TimeMAE masked-codeword classification, BERT/word2vec-style) over token sequences -> contextual token embeddings WITHOUT forecasting.

Intrinsic vocabulary scorecard: codebook utilization/perplexity + reconstruction MSE + usage Zipfian/dead-token rate + cross-asset token coverage + bits-per-bar compression -> the no-predictor quality gate.
warnings: REJECT 'Dynamic Tokenization via Reinforcement Patching' (arXiv:2603.26097): its variable-length patch boundaries are learned with a FORECASTING reward. It only works as a forecaster and violates our no-prediction rule. Tempting because it gives variable-length tokens — but the boundary signal is predictive; use BPE-frequency boundaries instead, which need no forecasting.

TOTEM as-published uses FIXED compression F=4 -> fixed-length tokens, NOT the variable-length tokens our spec requires. Borrow its non-predictive VQ training and per-channel-shared codebook, but you must add BPE/dynamic merging on top to get variable length.

TOTEM does NOT normalize inputs ('operate directly on time steps') -> a learned VQ on raw candles would key on absolute level/scale and BREAK cross-asset transfer. We MUST normalize / use relative encoding before encoding; this is a real gap to patch, not an optional nicety.

Plain VQ-VAE codebook collapse: without EMA + dead-code reset + entropy/utilization penalty, the learned vocabulary silently shrinks to a few codes and looks fine on reconstruction while being useless as a language. Always report codebook utilization/perplexity during training, not just loss.

Reconstruction fidelity alone is NOT sufficient evidence of a good vocabulary (a near-identity codebook can reconstruct well yet carry no recurring-shape semantics). Pair reconstruction with utilization AND cross-asset recurrence; otherwise you repeat the project's documented 'classifier-metric improves but the real objective doesn't' anti-correlation trap.

Contrastive Stage-2 (TS2Vec) depends heavily on the augmentation choice; for tokens, naive augmentations can create false positives (two genuinely different shapes treated as the same). Prefer masked-token recovery (TimeMAE) as the primary Stage-2 objective and treat contrastive as auxiliary only.

Pooling BPE statistics across all 64 assets assumes shapes are genuinely shared post-normalization; if one asset's microstructure dominates frequency counts it can bias the vocabulary. Check per-asset token-usage balance as part of the scorecard.

findings.lens: Making a price-action token vocabulary transferable across assets and filtered to "viable" tokens, with a prediction-free quality gate. The literature splits cleanly into our three concerns: (1) RELATIVE/PER-WINDOW encoding gives scale/offset/location invariance "for free" (matches our ratio-encoding claim that cross-asset transfer is a property, not learned attention); (2) GRAMMAR/MOTIF + SPARSE-DICTIONARY methods give variable-length recurring atoms and a principled way to keep only "viable" ones (matches "the trader ignores candle runs that aren't viable tokens"); (3) COMPRESSION/RECONSTRUCTION criteria (MDL, reconstruction error, vocabulary-overlap/reuse rates) give us a vocabulary-quality gate with NO downstream predictor.

methods.name: SAX + numerosity reduction (per-window z-normalized discretization)
methods.summary: SAX z-normalizes each window then maps PAA segment means to symbols via equiprobable Gaussian breakpoints, yielding a string invariant to amplitude and offset. Numerosity reduction collapses runs of identical symbols, which is exactly what produces VARIABLE-LENGTH segments and strips trivial/flat noise.
methods.borrow: Use per-window normalization as the invariance mechanism, but encode RELATIVE bar-to-bar RATIOS (log-returns of O/H/L/C) instead of z-scored levels so a token is invariant to price level/scale/location by construction (our core claim). Adopt numerosity reduction directly: collapse repeated micro-shapes so identical relative moves merge into one variable-length token and flat noise self-deletes. Keep the equiprobable-breakpoint idea but fit breakpoints on the empirical return distribution across all 64 assets so the same ratio maps to the same symbol on every asset.
methods.source: Lin et al., 'Experiencing SAX: a Novel Symbolic Representation of Time Series' (cs.gmu.edu/~jessica/SAX_DAMI_preprint.pdf); jmotif SAX algorithm page

methods.name: GrammarViz: SAX + Sequitur grammar induction for variable-length motifs
methods.summary: Discretize with SAX, then run Sequitur (linear-time CFG induction) on the symbol string. Grammar non-terminals = recurring substrings = variable-length motifs; rule frequency separates frequent rules (motifs/our viable tokens) from rare rules (anomalies/noise). Sequitur's 'utility constraint' guarantees every non-terminal corresponds to a genuinely recurrent pattern.
methods.borrow: This is the closest published analogue to our tokenizer. Pipeline: relative-ratio SAX string -> Sequitur/BPE-style induction -> the induced grammar rules ARE the token vocabulary, and they are inherently variable-length. Use rule frequency as the first viability filter: rules appearing >= N times across the 64-asset corpus are kept as tokens; one-off substrings are 'unviable' runs the trader ignores. The utility constraint gives a clean, parameter-light definition of 'recurring'.
methods.source: Senin et al., GrammarViz 2.0/3.0 (grammarviz2.github.io); 'Time series anomaly discovery with grammar-based compression' (openproceedings.org/2015/conf/edbt/paper-155.pdf)

methods.name: MDL intrinsic cardinality & dimensionality (parameter-free, prediction-free gate)
methods.summary: Choose alphabet size (symbol cardinality) and PAA length by minimizing description length = model bits + data-given-model bits. Genuine recurring structure compresses; noise does not. Fully unsupervised, no forecasting target.
methods.borrow: This is our vocabulary-quality GATE with NO predictor. Score a candidate vocabulary by total bits to encode the whole 64-asset corpus = (cost to store the codebook) + (cost to encode every series as a token sequence). A GOOD language lowers total bits vs raw/quantile baseline. Use MDL to auto-pick alphabet cardinality and the ratio-bucket count instead of hand-tuning, and to decide whether adding a candidate token to the vocabulary pays for itself (does it shrink total description length?). Directly replaces the discarded next-bar-sign probe.
methods.source: Hu, Rakthanmanon, Campana, Mueen, Keogh, 'Discovering the Intrinsic Cardinality and Dimensionality of Time Series' (cs.ucr.edu/~eamonn/ICDM_mdl.pdf); MDL-based time series clustering (Rakthanmanon/Keogh)

methods.name: K-SVD / sparse coding overcomplete dictionary of atoms
methods.summary: Learn an overcomplete dictionary so each signal window = sparse linear combination of a few atoms; alternate sparse-coding (OMP) and atom updates to minimize reconstruction error under an L0 sparsity budget. Atoms are the recurring 'shapes'.
methods.borrow: Gives a reconstruction-based notion of 'viable': an atom is viable if it is actually used (nonzero coefficient) in the sparse codes of many windows; atoms never selected by OMP are dead and get pruned. The sparsity budget operationalizes 'the trader ignores candle runs that don't map to a viable token' — a window whose best sparse reconstruction has large residual is NOT well-explained by the language and can be flagged unviable/noise. Train K-SVD on per-window-normalized relative-return segments so atoms are scale-invariant shapes shared across assets.
methods.source: Aharon, Elad, Bruckstein, 'K-SVD: An Algorithm for Designing Overcomplete Dictionaries for Sparse Representation' (IEEE TSP 2006); syanga/ksvd-sparse-dictionary

methods.name: Shapelet Dictionary Learning (generative shapelets)
methods.summary: Instead of searching subsequences in the data, LEARN a small dictionary of generative shapelets via dictionary learning; the learned atoms capture local shape features shared across many series and generalize better than mined subsequences.
methods.borrow: Supports building the vocabulary as a small LEARNED set of canonical relative-shapes rather than enumerating every observed subsequence — better generalization and cross-asset reuse, and naturally bounded vocabulary size. Use it as an alternative/refinement to grammar induction when raw motif enumeration over 64 assets is too large; the dictionary IS the token set.
methods.source: 'A Shapelet Dictionary Learning Algorithm for Time Series Classification' (IEEE, ieeexplore.ieee.org/document/8843231); Zhang et al. 2021 (Wiley, doi 10.1155/2021/5586273)

methods.name: WQ4TS shared 'wavebook' for cross-domain transfer
methods.summary: Cross-domain time series pretraining via Wave Quantization: every domain's series is projected onto ONE fixed, mathematically-derived wavelet basis ('wavebook') producing tokens in a common spectral space, giving strong zero-shot (+44%) and few-shot (+25%) transfer without per-domain codebook fitting.
methods.borrow: Key design lesson: a FIXED, non-learned, mathematically-principled token basis transfers across domains better and more cheaply than a learned per-domain VQ-VAE codebook — strong external support for our 'transfer is a property of the encoding, not learned' thesis. Validates choosing relative-ratio buckets (analogous to their fixed basis) over a learned cross-asset model. WARNING they note: they never SHOWED identical codes recur across domains — so we must measure reuse explicitly (see overlap metric below).
methods.source: Ma, Hong, Li, Lu, 'A Wave is Worth 100 Words: Investigating Cross-Domain Transferability in Time Series' (arXiv:2412.00772; ACM TKDD 10.1145/3788674)

methods.name: Vocabulary-overlap / token-reuse as the transferability metric
methods.summary: In multilingual LMs, transfer quality rises monotonically with shared-vocabulary OVERLAP between corpora; tokens with shared meaning across corpora drive transfer. Overlap is computed directly from token-id sets per corpus.
methods.borrow: This is our concrete, prediction-free transferability measurement. Build the vocabulary on a subset of assets, then for each held-out asset compute (a) token-id set overlap / Jaccard with the training vocabulary and (b) per-token reuse rate = fraction of held-out assets in which a token appears. A transferable language = high overlap and high cross-asset reuse for the bulk of tokens; tokens used on only one asset are non-transferable and candidates for pruning. Report a coverage curve: % of each held-out asset's stream explained by the shared vocabulary.
methods.source: 'False Friends Are Not Foes: Investigating Vocabulary Overlap in Multilingual Language Models' (arXiv:2509.18750); 'Overlap-based Vocabulary Generation Improves Cross-lingual Transfer' (arXiv:2203.01976)

methods.name: Small-vocabulary tokenization + token-space utilization (Cramer's V)
methods.summary: Systematic study of TS tokenizer design: scaling (mean/min-max/normal) x quantization (uniform/normal/exp-decay binning). Balanced token-space utilization (high Cramer's V, even token frequencies) correlates with downstream quality; small vocabularies transfer better when paired with pretraining.
methods.borrow: Two borrowable, prediction-free diagnostics: (1) measure token-frequency balance / utilization — a healthy vocabulary uses most tokens, with no dead tokens and no single token swallowing the stream (avoid the SAX failure where one symbol dominates flat markets); (2) prefer a SMALL vocabulary — it transfers better and keeps the downstream trader's token stream compressed. Use their binning insight: place ratio-bucket edges on the empirical return CDF (normal/quantile binning) so buckets are equiprobable and balanced across assets.
methods.source: 'Small Vocabularies, Big Gains: Pretraining and Tokenization in Time Series Models' (arXiv:2511.11622)

methods.name: Kinematic Tokenization: reconstruction-error token-quality criterion
methods.summary: Segments noisy time series into variable-length continuous-time tokens by fitting smooth dynamical-system trajectories; objective balances reconstruction fidelity, smoothness, and compressibility. Explicitly uses a PREDICTION-FREE quality metric: token quality = how well tokens reconstruct the input, independent of any downstream task.
methods.borrow: Direct endorsement of a reconstruction-based, no-predictor gate. Complement the MDL bit-count gate with a reconstruction-residual gate: a vocabulary is good if token sequences reconstruct the relative-return stream with low residual at a fixed token budget; windows with high residual are the 'noise runs' the trader should ignore. The fidelity+smoothness+compressibility triad is a good explicit objective shape for our tokenizer's segmentation step.
methods.source: 'Kinematic Tokenization: Optimization-Based Continuous-Time Tokens for Learnable Decision Policies in Noisy Time Series' (arXiv:2601.09949)

key_takeaways: Invariance should be BUILT IN by the encoding, not learned: per-window normalization (SAX z-norm; sliding-window min-max) plus relative/ratio features make a token invariant to price level, scale, and location by construction — exactly our thesis that cross-asset transfer is a property of the encoding, not cross-asset attention. WQ4TS independently confirms a fixed mathematical basis transfers across domains better than a learned per-domain codebook.

Variable-length recurring tokens are a SOLVED shape of problem: SAX+Sequitur (GrammarViz) induces a grammar whose non-terminals ARE variable-length recurring motifs, and its utility/frequency constraint already separates 'recurring = keep' from 'rare = noise/anomaly'. This is the closest published analogue to the tokenizer we want.

We have at least THREE legitimate prediction-free quality gates to replace the discarded next-bar-sign probe: (1) MDL total-description-length of the corpus under the vocabulary; (2) reconstruction residual at a fixed token budget (sparse-coding / kinematic tokenization); (3) cross-asset token-reuse / vocabulary-overlap on held-out assets. None forecast anything.

'Viable token' has a precise operational meaning across methods: a token/atom that is (a) frequent under the grammar/utility constraint, (b) actually selected in sparse reconstruction (OMP-used, not dead), and (c) reused across many assets. A candle run that maps to no viable token = high reconstruction residual / rare grammar rule = exactly the noise the trader should ignore.

Vocabulary should be SMALL and BALANCED: small vocabularies transfer better, and token-frequency balance (Cramer's V / utilization) is itself a prediction-free health metric. Watch for the SAX pathology where flat/low-vol regimes collapse to one dominant symbol.

Fit the discretization on the POOLED multi-asset return distribution (equiprobable / quantile bin edges) so the same relative move maps to the same token on every asset — this is what makes the '$225/unit vs $0.45/unit same token' example actually hold.
directly_applicable: Encode each bar as relative ratios (log-returns of O/H/L/C and per-bar range), per-window normalized, instead of absolute levels — the SAX/z-norm/min-max invariance result applied to our ratio claim.
Adopt SAX-style numerosity reduction to merge repeated micro-shapes into one variable-length token and auto-delete flat-noise runs.

Induce the vocabulary with a Sequitur/BPE-style grammar over the symbol stream; use grammar-rule frequency/utility as the first 'viable token' filter (frequent rule = token; one-off substring = ignored run).
Use MDL (model bits + data-given-model bits) over the 64-asset corpus as the primary prediction-free vocabulary-quality gate and to auto-select alphabet cardinality and ratio-bucket count.
Add a sparse-coding/K-SVD reconstruction view: prune dead atoms (never OMP-selected), and flag windows with high reconstruction residual as unviable/noise the trader skips.
Measure transferability directly as cross-asset token-reuse rate + held-out-asset vocabulary overlap (Jaccard) + stream-coverage curve — no predictor needed.
Fit equiprobable/quantile bin edges on the POOLED return distribution across all 64 assets so identical relative moves tokenize identically regardless of asset price scale.
Track token-frequency balance (utilization / Cramer's V) and keep the vocabulary small as standing health diagnostics.
warnings: SAX/PAA averaging within a segment can smear sharp OHLC moves and wicks; PAA segment means lose intra-bar high/low structure that is load-bearing for candlestick action. Encode wicks/ranges explicitly rather than only close-to-close means, or PAA will erase the very shapes we want to tokenize.

Per-window z-normalization amplifies noise in flat/low-volatility windows (dividing by near-zero std), producing spurious tokens and a dominant 'flat' symbol — the known SAX pathology. Guard the denominator (jnp.maximum on std/range) and consider a dedicated low-vol/flat token rather than forcing structure onto noise.

WQ4TS explicitly did NOT demonstrate that identical codes recur across domains — 'should transfer' is not 'does transfer'. Do not assume cross-asset reuse; measure it (overlap/reuse metrics) or the central transferability claim is unverified.

MDL and reconstruction gates reward COMPRESSION, not usefulness. A vocabulary can minimize bits/residual yet be useless to the trader (e.g., it perfectly encodes noise textures). These gates prove the language is well-formed and recurring, not that tokens carry tradeable meaning — keep that strictly downstream (stage 2/3), but be aware a low-bit vocabulary is necessary, not sufficient.

Pure subsequence/motif enumeration over 64 assets at minute granularity is huge; naive variable-length motif search is expensive. Prefer linear-time grammar induction (Sequitur) or generative shapelet-dictionary learning over brute-force enumeration (HIME/DP-Sequitur exist for scale but add complexity).

The financial shapelet framework (2509.15040) bakes in supervised/label-driven viability (K-S test, purity threshold, canonical chart-pattern seeds) — do NOT borrow those parts; they reintroduce prediction/labels we are explicitly removing. Borrow only its unsupervised per-window min-max normalization and DTW-cluster shape grouping.

Token-frequency imbalance is easy to hit: equiprobable binning balances symbols but a few grammar rules can still dominate. Monitor utilization; a vocabulary where one token covers most of the stream is failing even if MDL looks fine.

findings.lens: Judge a price-action tokenizer's vocabulary WITHOUT any downstream predictor or forecast, by treating the tokenizer as (a) a lossy compressor of one asset's minute-candle stream into recurring relative-shape symbols and (b) a discrete code over a corpus. The vocabulary is "right" if it COMPRESSES well (MDL), COVERS most of the stream, RECONSTRUCTS each segment within the relative-shape tolerance, uses its CODEBOOK efficiently (balanced Zipf/Rényi, high perplexity, few dead codes), SEGMENTS STABLY under perturbation, and RECURS ACROSS ASSETS (transfer overlap) — all measurable on raw token streams with zero labels and zero prediction. The discarded next-bar-sign probe was a forecast metric and is correctly thrown out; every metric below is intrinsic/self-supervised.

methods.name: Two-part MDL description length (Krimp 'code table' formulation)
methods.summary: The best pattern/vocabulary set is the one that compresses the data most: total cost = L(model) + L(data | model) in bits. Krimp builds a 'code table' (pattern -> Shannon code by usage frequency) and scores a candidate vocabulary by total compressed size; a smaller set of high-usage patterns wins over thousands of frequent ones.
methods.borrow: Make total description length the SINGLE headline metric. Define L(tokens) = sum over the stream of -log2 p(token) (Shannon code by empirical token usage) + L(codebook) = sum over vocab of bits to store each token's relative-shape template (length + per-bar ratio quantized). Compare against two baselines: (1) raw-candle entropy coder (must beat it -> the language actually compresses), (2) a trivial fixed-length n-gram tokenizer (must beat it -> the variable-length recurring shapes earn their keep). PASS: total bits-per-candle strictly below both baselines, and adding more vocab entries stops reducing total DL (the L(model) term overtakes the L(data) gain) — that knee IS the right vocab size, chosen with no prediction.
methods.source: Vreeken, van Leeuwen, Siebes, 'Krimp: mining itemsets that compress', DMKD 2011 — https://link.springer.com/content/pdf/10.1007/s10618-010-0202-x.pdf ; MDL principle overview http://www.modelselection.org/mdl/

methods.name: Grammar-based compression size (Re-Pair / Sequitur)
methods.summary: Re-Pair repeatedly replaces the most frequent adjacent pair with a new rule; Sequitur maintains a context-free grammar enforcing digram-uniqueness and rule-utility. Final grammar size (number of rules + total rule length) is a direct, predictor-free measure of how repetitive/compressible a sequence is; storing d rules costs ~ d log d + 0.557d bits.
methods.borrow: Run Re-Pair on the token-ID stream (tokens as terminals) per asset. If a good language exists, frequent token bigrams collapse into a compact grammar -> small grammar size relative to stream length. Use grammar size as a cheap, parameter-light sanity proxy for MDL, AND as a guard against over-fragmentation: a vocab that is just noise yields a grammar barely smaller than the input. Watch the 'too many nonterminals inflates bit-size' warning — if grammar size grows when you enlarge the vocab, the vocab is adding noise tokens.
methods.source: Larsson & Moffat Re-Pair; Nevill-Manning & Witten Sequitur; entropy bounds for grammar compression, Gańczorz 2018 https://arxiv.org/pdf/1804.08547 ; https://www.mdpi.com/1999-4893/5/2/214

methods.name: Coverage of the stream by the vocabulary
methods.summary: Fraction of the input series explained by assigned motifs/tokens vs. left as un-encoded residual/fallback. In Krimp-style cover and in motif-set evaluation, coverage measures how much of the data the pattern set accounts for; high coverage with a compact set is the goal.
methods.borrow: Define coverage = fraction of candles that belong to an emitted (non-fallback) token. Our pipeline INTENTIONALLY drops noise runs that map to no viable token, so coverage will not be 100% — but report it explicitly and set a floor. PASS: coverage in a sensible band (e.g. >= 60-70% of candles tokenized) AND fallback/UNK rate bounded (e.g. < 25%). Too-low coverage = the language misses real structure; ~100% coverage = it is tokenizing noise and the denoising payoff is gone. Pair coverage with mean token length (candles/token = the 'fertility'/compression-rate analogue): report bits-per-candle and candles-per-token together.
methods.source: Quantitative evaluation of motif sets in time series, DMKD 2025 https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s10618-025-01169-5 ; coverage/fallback as in swiss-ai 'Vocabulary Utilization' & 'UNK Token Rate' https://github.com/swiss-ai/tokenizer-intrinsic-evals

methods.name: Reconstruction fidelity within the relative-shape tolerance (SAX lower-bounding discretization)
methods.summary: SAX maps a real series to symbols via PAA + quantile binning and is the canonical lossy-but-bounded symbolization; quality is judged by reconstruction/quantization error (MSE) and by tightness of the symbolic distance as a lower bound on the true distance. Lloyd-Max/KDE binning minimizes information loss in the discretization step.
methods.borrow: Since a token is defined by RELATIVE per-bar ratios with a tolerance, measure reconstruction error in ratio space: for every tokenized segment, reconstruct the candle ratios from the token's canonical template and compute the relative error (e.g. max |log(actual_ratio/template_ratio)|). PASS: a high fraction (e.g. >= 90-95%) of token occurrences reconstruct within the declared tolerance, with bounded mean ratio-MSE. This certifies the vocabulary is granular enough to be faithful without forecasting. Use Lloyd-Max/quantile binning (not equiprobable-Gaussian) to set the ratio bins so high-density move ranges get finer codes.
methods.source: Lin et al. SAX (lower-bounding property); 'Distribution Agnostic Symbolic Representations' https://arxiv.org/pdf/2105.09592 ; Lloyd-Max/KDE binning https://www.emergentmind.com/topics/symbolic-aggregate-approximation-sax

methods.name: Codebook utilization & perplexity (VQ-VAE)
methods.summary: Codebook perplexity = exp(-sum p_i log p_i) over code-usage probabilities = the 'effective number of codes used'; equals vocab size when usage is uniform, 1 when collapsed. Codebook collapse / dead codes (codes with near-zero usage) is the standard failure mode and is measured directly as the active-code fraction.
methods.borrow: Treat the vocabulary as a codebook. Report: (1) active-code fraction = tokens used >= k times / |V|; (2) perplexity / |V| (normalized effective usage). PASS: active fraction high (e.g. > 80%) and normalized perplexity not tiny -> no collapse, no swarm of dead tokens. This is a pure usage statistic, zero prediction. If perplexity is near 1, a few mega-tokens dominate (under-segmented); if active fraction is low, the vocab is bloated with never-fired shapes (prune them).
methods.source: VQ-VAE perplexity definition & codebook-collapse literature https://www.emergentmind.com/topics/vector-quantization-variational-autoencoder-vq-vae ; index-collapse measurement https://arxiv.org/html/2406.02940v1

methods.name: Distributional shape: Zipfianness + Rényi efficiency of the unigram token distribution
methods.summary: A natural 'language' has Zipfian token frequencies. Fit log-frequency vs log-rank: report Zipf slope, rank-frequency AUC, and mean abs deviation from the power-law fit. Rényi efficiency Eff_alpha = H_alpha / log|V| with H_alpha = (1/(1-alpha)) log(sum p_w^alpha); Zouhar's recommended alpha ~ 2.5-3; it penalizes BOTH over-frequent and over-rare tokens and correlated ~0.78 with downstream BLEU vs -0.32 for raw compressed length.
methods.borrow: Compute on the token stream: Zipf slope (target a clean power law, slope near -1, low deviation-from-fit), and Rényi efficiency at alpha=2.5. PASS: token frequencies are approximately Zipfian (low MAE from log-log linear fit) and Rényi efficiency sits in a healthy mid band (not maximized — see warnings). This catches the two pathologies a price tokenizer hits: (a) one giant 'flat/doji' token swamping everything (low efficiency, broken Zipf) and (b) thousands of near-unique tokens (degenerate uniform). Report it as a diagnostic of distribution HEALTH, never as a score to maximize.
methods.source: Zouhar et al. 'Tokenization and the Noiseless Channel' (Rényi efficiency, alpha, BLEU corr) https://arxiv.org/pdf/2306.16842 ; Zipf/AUC/slope/deviation operationalized in 'Beyond Text Compression' https://aclanthology.org/2025.acl-long.1546.pdf

methods.name: Segmentation stability / boundary consistency under perturbation
methods.summary: Stability is measured by how consistent the segmentation/labeling is under small input perturbations, with no ground-truth labels needed — analogous to unsupervised temporal-consistency metrics for video segmentation and image-segmentation stability studies. Boundary precision/recall quantify boundary agreement between two segmentations.
methods.borrow: Re-tokenize a window under tiny, shape-preserving perturbations: add sub-tolerance price jitter, shift the window start by a few bars, rescale absolute price (must be a no-op given relative encoding!). Then measure agreement between the original and perturbed token sequences: boundary F1 (do segment boundaries land in the same places) and token-label agreement on overlapping spans. The price-rescale invariance test is a CRITICAL, free correctness gate — by construction it must yield identical tokens; any disagreement is a bug in the relative encoding. PASS: rescale agreement ~100%; jitter/shift boundary-F1 high (e.g. > 0.9). This is the direct, principled replacement for the next-bar probe — it tests that the language is a stable, level/scale/position-invariant function of shape.
methods.source: Unsupervised Temporal Consistency Metric for Video Segmentation, CVPRW 2020 https://openaccess.thecvf.com/content_CVPRW_2020/papers/w20/Varghese_Unsupervised_Temporal_Consistency_Metric_for_Video_Segmentation_in_Highly-Automated_Driving_CVPRW_2020_paper.pdf ; Image Segmentation Stability empirical study http://schoolofcomputing.southalabama.edu/~cbrown/brown2018image.pdf

methods.name: Cross-asset recurrence / vocabulary transfer overlap
methods.summary: In cross-lingual transfer, shared-vocabulary overlap between corpora predicts transfer; overlap is quantified as the fraction of tokens (or token-mass) shared across the two vocabularies/streams, and disjoint vocabularies cause large transfer drops. This is computed purely on token statistics, no model.
methods.borrow: This is THE existence proof for our core claim that relative encoding gives cross-asset transferability as a PROPERTY. Build the vocabulary on asset A; tokenize asset B with the SAME codebook and measure: (1) mass-weighted overlap = fraction of B's candles covered by tokens that also fire on A; (2) Jaccard of the active high-frequency vocab between A and B; (3) frequency-rank correlation (Spearman) of shared tokens across assets. PASS: held-out assets at totally different price levels ($225 vs $0.45) show high coverage and high rank-correlation with the build asset. If overlap is low, the encoding is NOT actually level/scale-invariant in practice -> the central design promise fails, regardless of single-asset MDL. Critically, this validates transfer WITHOUT cross-asset attention and WITHOUT prediction.
methods.source: Patil et al. 'Overlap-based Vocabulary Generation Improves Cross-lingual Transfer' https://arxiv.org/abs/2203.01976 ; token-overlap vs transfer https://arxiv.org/pdf/2509.18750

key_takeaways: Reframe the whole problem as lossy compression + discrete coding, NOT classification or forecasting. Every metric here is computable from raw token streams with zero labels — this fully and legitimately replaces the next-bar-sign probe, which was a forecast metric and rightly discarded.

Make total two-part MDL (bits-per-candle = code-the-data + code-the-codebook) the single headline number, and let its knee SELECT the vocabulary size automatically. Everything else is a diagnostic that explains WHY a vocab does or does not compress.

Our 'token = recurring variable-length relative-shape run' is formally a time-series MOTIF / grammar RULE / itemset-cover. That means the mature, predictor-free machinery (Krimp MDL, Re-Pair/Sequitur grammar size, motif-set coverage, SAX bounded reconstruction) maps onto us directly and is the right literature, not LLM-tokenizer folklore.

Three checks form an irreducible 'is the language right' triangle: (1) compression — MDL beats raw-candle and fixed n-gram baselines; (2) fidelity — segments reconstruct within the relative-shape tolerance (e.g. >=90-95%); (3) invariance/stability — identical tokens under absolute-price rescale and high boundary-F1 under sub-tolerance jitter. A vocab can ace one and fail another; require all three.

The absolute-price-rescale invariance test is a free, must-pass correctness gate that follows directly from the relative-ratio definition: rescaling the price MUST produce byte-identical tokens. Run it first — it is the cheapest way to catch encoding bugs before any expensive metric.

Cross-asset recurrence overlap (build vocab on asset A, score coverage + frequency-rank correlation on asset B at a wildly different price level) is the direct, non-predictive existence proof for the project's central claim that transferability is a PROPERTY of relative encoding rather than learned cross-asset attention.

Distribution-shape metrics (Zipf slope, Rényi efficiency at alpha~2.5, codebook perplexity/active-code fraction) are HEALTH diagnostics with target BANDS, never quantities to maximize — maximizing them is provably gameable (see warnings).
directly_applicable: Total description length in bits-per-candle (two-part MDL: -log2 p(token) summed over stream + bits to store each token's relative-shape template). Headline metric. PASS: strictly below both a raw-candle entropy coder and a fixed-length n-gram tokenizer; pick vocab size at the DL knee.
Coverage = fraction of candles assigned to a non-fallback token; report alongside UNK/fallback rate. PASS band: coverage >=60-70% AND fallback <25% (noise is meant to be dropped, so NOT 100%).
Mean candles-per-token (compression rate / fertility analogue) — report jointly with coverage and bits-per-candle so under- vs over-segmentation is visible.

Reconstruction fidelity in ratio space: fraction of token occurrences whose reconstructed per-bar ratios fall within the declared tolerance. PASS: >=90-95% within tolerance, bounded mean log-ratio MSE.
Codebook active-code fraction (tokens used >= k times / |V|) and normalized perplexity (effective-codes / |V|). PASS: active fraction >80%, perplexity not collapsed toward 1.
Zipf diagnostics on token frequencies: log-log slope (target near -1), rank-frequency AUC, mean-abs-deviation from power-law fit. Diagnostic band, not maximized.
Rényi efficiency Eff_alpha = H_alpha/log|V| at alpha=2.5. Report as a mid-band health check only (do NOT optimize).
Absolute-price-rescale invariance: re-tokenize the same window at a different price scale; token sequence MUST be identical. Hard PASS = 100% agreement (it is a correctness gate, not a soft metric).
Segmentation stability under sub-tolerance jitter and small window shifts: boundary-F1 and overlapping-span token agreement between original and perturbed tokenizations. PASS: boundary-F1 > 0.9.

Cross-asset transfer overlap: build vocab on asset A, apply codebook to asset B (very different price level); report mass-weighted coverage of B, active-vocab Jaccard, and Spearman frequency-rank correlation of shared tokens. PASS: high coverage + high rank correlation on held-out assets.
Re-Pair/Sequitur grammar size on the token-ID stream as a cheap repetitiveness/over-fragmentation sanity proxy backing the MDL number.
warnings: Do NOT maximize Rényi efficiency. Zouhar et al.'s own follow-up ('Two Counterexamples to Tokenization and the Noiseless Channel') proves it is gameable: random-drop BPE and duplication BPE both RAISE Rényi efficiency while DEGRADING downstream quality. Use it only as a mid-band health diagnostic, never as an objective.

Compression alone is not sufficient and can be adversarially optimized — a tokenizer can shrink token count while becoming worse. Always pair MDL/compression with fidelity (reconstruction within tolerance) and stability; the same paper shows compressed-length correlated only -0.32 with downstream quality vs 0.78 for a balanced metric.

Boundary-alignment style metrics (the MorphScore analogue) are known to explain little variance once scale is controlled (multiple 2025 morphological-alignment studies). Treat our boundary/segmentation metrics as STABILITY checks, not as proof the vocabulary is semantically meaningful — meaning is deferred to Stage 2 by design.

100% coverage / near-1 Zipf perfection is a red flag, not success: it usually means the tokenizer is symbolizing noise, which destroys the denoising/efficiency payoff that motivates the whole token pipeline. Want high coverage of STRUCTURE with explicit noise rejection.

Adding vocabulary almost always reduces L(data|model) and improves naive 'compression'; the MODEL term L(codebook) is what stops over-fragmentation. If you only track data-coding bits (not the two-part total), you will pick a bloated, dead-code-ridden vocabulary. The grammar-size 'too many nonterminals inflates bits' result is the same warning from the grammar-compression side.

SAX-style reconstruction with default equiprobable-Gaussian bins assumes a distribution minute-candle ratios do not follow (heavy tails, fat moves). Use Lloyd-Max/quantile/KDE binning to set ratio bins, or fidelity numbers will be misleadingly bad on exactly the large-move shapes that matter most.

Cross-asset overlap can look high for a trivial reason — if a single 'flat/doji' token dominates, it will recur everywhere and inflate overlap while carrying no information. Always report overlap EXCLUDING the top-1/top-k mega-tokens, and check rank-correlation of the mid-frequency tokens, not just raw coverage.

Most surveyed metrics come from NLP/CV/itemset domains with NO published numeric thresholds (the 'Beyond Text Compression' paper explicitly gives none). The PASS numbers proposed here are reasoned starting points to be CALIBRATED on our own data via the MDL knee and baseline comparisons, not literature-certified constants — do not present them as established.
